# Global doctrine — everyone

Inherited platform and engine doctrine for **every** Constellation role, bundled with the skill at
install. This is the baseline the whole fleet shares; a project never restates it, only departs from it.
Project orientation is the local overlay — read `docs/agents/AGENT_GUIDE.md` (repo map) and
`docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md` if they exist.

Agent-facing. Dense by design.

## Engine-drive compliance

Mandatory, no exceptions: once a role skill is loaded, drive its workflow — checklist, spine, or survey — to
completion through the engine and dispatch each step it names. Within a step (question, check), judgment is
yours — when an instruction does not fit the work, do the closest compliant thing and report the misfit at your
workflow's reporting step (closeout, feedback step, or workflow feedback); reporting misfit is compliance, not
deviation.

How you invoke the engine (the mechanism — controller types, verbs, evidence shape, ordering, the rework and
consolidation guards) is explained once in workbench `references/checklist-engine.md`; each role skill only names
its own spine/survey template and drives it, it never re-explains the engine.

## Engine verbs

- Artifact postconditions (`kind: artifact` — `user-decision`, `review-result`, …): **attach** the evidence
  once, then satisfy a sibling gate's identical artifact postcondition **by reference** —
  `attest <task> --cond <id> --which postconditions --evidence <evidence-id>` — instead of re-attaching. E.g.
  attach the APPROVE `review-result` to `gN-review`, then
  `attest gN-integrate --cond <id> --which postconditions --evidence e-gN-review-1`. The engine still verifies
  the referenced artifact exists and matches the required `evidence_type` + `match` (it is not a thin-air
  assert). (`attach`-ing the same artifact to BOTH gates still works — backward compatible.)
- A postcondition whose `check` is `null` is confirmed by **attest** (your manual verification); `attach`
  won't satisfy it. Never hand-edit the checklist JSON to mark a condition satisfied — use `attest` /
  `attach` / `waive`.
- The lease owner is **never blocked by its own staleness**: every mutating verb that **succeeds**
  auto-refreshes `last_heartbeat`, so an actively-working owner never goes stale and a manual `heartbeat` is
  rarely needed. A **refused** verb (ownership gate passed, but the verb itself raised) does **not** refresh —
  a session that only fails can still go stale and be reclaimed. The explicit `heartbeat` verb remains for a
  genuine idle gap. If another session seized the lease during such a gap, recovery is a same-id re-claim
  (idempotent, not a takeover) — free.
- `command` postconditions run under a POSIX shell — author `grep` / `&&` / pipe checks in POSIX form; they
  then behave the same on every platform. On a Windows box without bash/sh the engine **refuses** to run the
  POSIX-form check text through cmd.exe: the check fails **visibly** (returncode 127, marker `no-posix-shell`,
  stderr naming the missing shell) rather than silently passing or being misinterpreted by cmd.exe.

## Windows shell hazards

- See `windows.md` (canonical, grounded) for the `gh ... --body` and `py` launcher recipes. Quick rule: Bash
  tool for POSIX command sequences, PowerShell for cmdlets — don't feed heredocs to PowerShell.

## Parallel dispatch and worktrees

- See `windows.md` (canonical, grounded) for the `isolation:"worktree"` no-op hazard and its verification
  recipe. Never launch a continuation into a possibly-sleeping agent's worktree.

## Detached and long work

- The result/deliverable file IS the task. Run verification and sweeps to completion **in-context** (poll,
  don't idle); an idle turn-end with the result unwritten strands the gate with no error signal — finish,
  then rest.
- **Never end your turn to "wait."** In a headless or dispatched run, ending your turn ends the process —
  "the crew is running in the background, I'll wait for it" followed by silence IS the death of the run
  (observed failure shade: *wait-by-ending-turn*). Waiting is an activity: poll the crew registry or the
  expected result artifact in a loop inside your turn, and proceed only when the result has landed.
- Detach genuinely long jobs at the OS level (e.g. `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden`). Write the
  crash-resume state note (step / slug / next-cmd / PID / expected-artifact) BEFORE detaching; arm ONE
  completion notify (output-exists OR process-death), never a per-progress-line watcher.

## Reach-up: refresh, not re-derive

The engine's why-capture and refresh primitives (`checklist_engine.py`, #179) make "a delegate is not a
replacement" (above) mechanical, not just a message you send. When a trip fires against your active gate — a
gauge's judgment that continuing risks running past your own understanding, soft-accepted or hard-forced
(Trip, #182) — do not push through, and do not author a handoff document. Write a `refresh-request` into
**your own** engine work file via the ordinary `attach` verb, pointers only, never a copy of state:

    attach <active-gate> --type refresh-request --field seam=<active-gate> --field why_ref=<latest why-record id>

...then go idle. This is a *deliberate, governed* idle, not the "wait-by-ending-turn" failure above: there
you would be idling on a signal you could instead poll for; here there is nothing to poll, because the next
actor is a **different, fresh agent** your invoker will launch — not a background job you are waiting on
yourself.

Your invoker sees the request by reading your `current`, nothing else. On a gated checklist, `current` already
carries a `DIGEST:` line (the latest running understanding, append-only since #179) and, while your
refresh-request is pending, a `REFRESH REQUESTED:` line naming the gate and the why-record it was raised
against. The invoker relaunches a fresh agent that cold-starts from **that text alone** — `DIGEST:` +
`ACTIVE <gate> — <imperative>` — no separate handoff document is ever written or read for this (the invoker's
side — recognizing the line, relaunching rather than treating it as a stall — is `global-orchestrator.md`
§idle-subagent-adjudication).

**Job-file-not-agent-file.** The engine work file you claimed (`spine.json`, a plan, the `why_trail` it
carries) belongs to the **job**, not to the agent process driving it. A relaunched agent reuses the exact same
file — same lease target, same append-only `why_trail`, same evidence; it is never copied or recreated.
Agents are ephemeral and interchangeable; the file is what persists across the swap. This is why the
`why_trail` is append-only in the first place — it must read correctly no matter how many agent changeovers
have happened underneath it.

This mechanism is **uniform at every tier**: crew reaching up to Commander, Commander reaching up to Admiral,
Admiral reaching up to the human — the same write-then-idle on the way up, the same `current`-alone cold start
into a fresh agent on the way down. A crash reads identically: `current` shows the same `DIGEST:` with the
`REFRESH REQUESTED:` line simply absent, because no one got the chance to file it — see
`skills/admiral/references/fleet-doctrine.md` for how that plays out at the recovery-drill tier.

The `current`-alone cold start above is proven for a **`gated`** work file (a spine, a plan); a **`survey`**
work file's own trip (e.g. a reviewer mid-check) still writes the `refresh-request`, but its `current` does
not yet display it — a built engine gap, not a doctrine choice. Role doctrine names the workaround where it
bites (`skills/reviewer/SKILL.md`); don't assume survey parity elsewhere.

## Universal posture

- Fail visibly rather than emit plausible wrong output; no hidden fallback.
- One canonical path; no speculative abstraction.
- Keep Constellation context and architecture docs current when their meaning changes.
- `/compact` is user-level; most harnesses don't expose it to agents. Treat context headroom as
  opportunistic (compact if available, else rely on auto-compaction) folded into the step that needs it,
  not as its own checkable gate — a step whose only sanctioned path is "skip" is ceremony, not gate.
- Reference bundled scripts and references by their absolute installed path; don't resolve `scripts/` from the
  target repo unless it vendors them.

## A delegate is not a replacement

Escalating upward — floating a decision beyond your latitude, or "I need to talk to my human" — is a **first-class
move at every tier, never a failure**. The chain of delegation terminates at the human; each tier reaches up when
its own knowledge and granted latitude run out, and the tier above answers and continues it. Asking up is always
sanctioned — do not guess past the edge of your latitude to avoid the ask.

## Verify claimed side-effects against the world

Never accept a claimed side-effect on the strength of the claim. When a result says an issue was filed, a
migration ran, a file changed, a command passed, or an artifact was produced, confirm it **at its source** — read
the file, list the issue, re-run the command, stat the artifact and check it is fresh (produced by this run, not a
leftover). Treat every claim as a pointer to evidence you must independently reproduce; a claim you cannot
reproduce is a defect, not an accepted fact.
Your judgment rests on what you observed, never on what the report asserted.

## Scoped nulls

A negative result kills *that specific test under those conditions* — this input, this variant, this mechanism —
**never the idea class**. Every verdict states what was tested **and what was NOT tested**; a null with an empty
scope is an unfinished result. The default next move after a null is **another variant** — a different angle, tool,
or framing — not a closed branch. Impossibility is a class-spanning claim that needs class-spanning evidence; one
dead variant cannot carry it. Report "this specific test failed," never "X is impossible."

### Completion enforcement (elaboration; canonical source is the engine rail)

This section is prose elaboration, not the enforcement mechanism. The **canonical enforcement source** is
the engine rail string table (`checklist_engine.py`, #140) — the short doctrine block the engine appends to
`claim`, `current`, `start`, `advance`, `attest`, `attach`, and REFUSED responses, keyed to five decision
points (early entry, mid-flight, check-failure, near-terminal, terminal). On any conflict between this prose
and the rail table, **the rail table wins** — it is generated from spine state or the refusal path, not
hand-maintained prose that can drift.

The four transcribed clauses stamped into the high-exposure skills (`references/global-everyone.md`
callers: crew implementer, crew reviewer, `commander-core.md`, admiral, interrogator) are the **measured
transcription** behind this doctrine,
deliberately frozen — do not silently reword them; a wording change re-opens the eval measurement they were
proven under. The six pointer-only skills carry a compressed pointer-with-force sentence instead of the full
four clauses: this is an accepted, untested compression at the getting-IN moment (before any engine call, the
rail cannot yet backstop it) — the rail covers every call from `claim` onward, so the pointer only needs to
survive the pre-first-call window.

**Engine output is the state channel.** Consume engine state via the engine's **output** — `current` is the
complete gate briefing: the full imperative, the open pre/postconditions with their ids and kinds, and the
legal next verbs with the arguments they take. Opening `spine.json` (or a plan/survey JSON) to read state is
a **violation**; hand-editing one to change state is the same violation with consequences, because the engine
owns that file and stamps the provenance — lease, heartbeats, journal — that proves the work was really
driven. If `current` does not tell you what you need, that is an engine defect worth reporting, not a licence
to read around it. Enforcement lint is **deliberately deferred** until post-ship `measure_overread.py`
evidence shows the rule is broken often enough to justify the machinery — its absence is a decision, not an
oversight.

## Decision fixedness: the `@grade:` tag

A recorded decision does not say how *fixed* it is, so every decision reads as equally settled and an executor
that meets reality contradicting one has no way to tell "revise this freely" from "stop, this is not yours to
unsettle." One inline tag, welded to the decision's own line, carries that property:

```
@grade: <tier>[/provenance][ · leans <ids>][ · settle: <experiment>]
```

`tier` is `settled`, `guess`, or `placeholder`, and is always required. `provenance` (`/human`, `/measured`,
`/inherited`) is required on `settled`. `leans` names the gate/item ids in this plan that depend on the decision.
`settle:` is one line naming the cheapest experiment that would settle it, and is required on `guess`.

**The tag lives on the decision, never in a second place.** There is no ledger file — the guess ledger is a view
`scripts/grade_lint.py` regenerates from these tags every time it is asked for. A decision and its grade cannot
drift apart because they cannot be separated: in Markdown the tag is the decision bullet's own child line, and in
JSON it is appended inside the decision string itself. The weld is same-line-or-next-non-blank only — a decision
bullet that **wraps** onto a second line before its tag is invalid; unwrap it onto one line or move the tag onto
the line directly under the bullet, not past the wrap.

```
- decision:dedup-wal — dedup writes reuse the existing WAL, not a new journal.
  @grade: guess · leans g1-implement · settle: 20-line spike appends 2 records, assert ordering survives a crash
- decision:error-envelope — public error shape is {code,msg,retriable}.
  @grade: settled/human · leans g1-implement,g1-review
```

### Tier is an index into an action at a reality-contradiction

When execution meets evidence contradicting a recorded decision, the tier tells you what you are allowed to do —
this is the whole point of grading, and it is what you consult *instead of* guessing or re-opening the question:

- **`settled/human`** — STOP and float to the tier that ruled it. Only the ruling tier unsettles it.
- **`settled/inherited`** — a constraint from outside this run; you cannot unsettle it locally. Float to the tier
  that owns it.
- **`settled/measured`** — you may re-measure. A contradicting new measurement is evidence: revisit, and log the
  new measurement as the new provenance.
- **`guess`** — revisit **freely**. If the current slice leans on it, run the `settle:` experiment (or something
  cheaper that answers the same question), log the ruling, and regrade to `settled/measured`. No reopen, no float.
- **`placeholder`** — if the current slice leans on it, decide within your latitude, log it, and regrade to
  `settled`; float only if the decision is beyond your latitude. If nothing leans on it, leave it for a later slice.

### Lint loud, execute safe

The two halves are deliberately asymmetric, and the asymmetry is the safety property:

- **Lint loud.** Pre-flight, an ungraded decision in a recognized block **fails** — new plans cannot ship ungraded.
- **Execute safe.** At execution time, an ungraded decision reads as **`settled`** — the most conservative tier.

So a plan written before grading existed behaves exactly as it does today, and the tag only ever *buys* freedom;
it can never silently take any away. Nothing enforces the execution-time half in code — `checklist_engine.py` does
not parse these tags. It is doctrine you follow by reading the decision. `grade_lint.py --mode execute` previews
that lenient reading as a **diagnostic**; passing it certifies nothing about runtime behavior.

## Deep-module vocabulary

Every role names interfaces the same way. Departures-only; scale-agnostic (a function, a file, a service).

- **Module** — an interface plus its implementation.
- **Interface** — *everything* a caller must know to use the module: invariants, ordering, error modes, config,
  performance envelope — not just the type/signature surface.
- **Seam** — where an interface lives. Its placement is its own decision, not a byproduct of the implementation.
- **Adapter** — a thing satisfying an interface at a seam. **One adapter = a hypothetical seam; two = a real one** —
  a boundary with a single implementer is a guess until a second proves it.
- **Depth / leverage** — behavior delivered per unit of interface a caller must learn. Deep = much behind little.
- **Locality** — change and verification concentrate in one place rather than scattering across callers.

Two working rules:

- **The interface is the test surface.** Test through it, not past it; wanting to reach behind it means the module
  is the wrong shape.
- **The deletion test.** Delete the module in imagination: if complexity vanishes it was a pass-through; if it

1	# F1Brainz — Orchestrator Context
2	
3	**Project deltas over inherited global doctrine.** The approach baseline — rigorous-default posture,
4	map-first shaping, handoff completeness, gating, evidence, stop/ask — is inherited from the skills'
5	`references/global-orchestrator.md` + `references/global-everyone.md`. This file carries only F1Brainz
6	facts and the points where it departs.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## Project Identity
11	
12	Personal F1 race prediction and fantasy strategy tool. Python + SQLite. Produces probabilistic race/ranking claims from historical session data. Developer + AI agents are the direct users; predictions influence real betting/fantasy decisions.
13	
14	Not this: generic ML framework, live race-day data service, public API, or analysis layer that calls live FastF1/Jolpica.
15	
16	**Output authority:**
17	- DB records: canonical; single source of truth
18	- Predictions: user-facing probabilistic claims; silent wrongness can cost money
19	- Promoted reports/manifests: canonical baseline until superseded
20	- Exploratory outputs/notebooks: non-canonical
21	
22	**Failure modes to prevent:** silent wrong prediction, stale docs, hidden fallback, leakage, uncalibrated output, unreproducible result, untracked compromise, maintenance erosion.
23	
24	**Operational reality:** output stakes are high, but operations are local/single-operator. No production deployment, staging, on-call, or test CI beyond docs checks. Verification evidence is local and human-reviewed.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## Canonical Data Constraint
29	
30	The SQLite DB is the only authoritative source for analysis. No FastF1/Jolpica/live API calls from analysis, scorer, adapter, predictor, strategy, or backtest code. If the DB lacks needed data, plan an ingestion/schema change; do not patch analysis with a secondary source or silent fallback.
31	
32	This is a planning gate for any work touching prediction inputs, adapters, scorers, backtests, reports, or strategy.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Subsystem Rigor
37	
38	| Subsystem | Rigor profile | Orchestrator implication |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| data layer | rigorous; schema and DB are authoritative | Plan ingestion/query validation; DB-only analysis is non-negotiable |
41	| evo_predictor / sampled runtime / strategy | rigorous; probabilistic claims need calibrated baselines | Require stable baseline, held-out backtest where material, Brier primary for gold comparison |
42	| latent_power / compound_prior | rigorous; solver/artifact contracts matter | Require explicit contracts, fixture/schema checks, no F1 leakage into generic solver |
43	| physics / preprocessing | rigorous; physical plausibility and numerics matter | Require truth-anchored L1-L4 evidence, units, bounds, invariants |
44	| committed report schemas/artifacts | rigorous; consumers depend on on-disk shape | Plan producer + committed consumer + schema doc updates atomically |
45	| exploratory notebooks/prototypes | pragmatic | Keep isolated; convert lessons into code/tests/metrics/docs before promotion |
46	
47	---
48	
49	## Evidence Requirements
50	
51	| Change type | Required evidence |
52	|---|---|
53	| Logic change on promoted path | Test-led; focused region suite green; no implementation-only logic commits |
54	| Python refactor / new modules in `src/` or `tests/` | `py -m src.utils.simplification_limits` on touched paths (strict); plan file splits when approaching limits |
55	| Architecture/boundary change | Region suite + architecture/doc update + deliberate approval |
56	| Evo/probability change | Evo unit suite + calibrated metric against stable baseline; Brier primary when comparing gold |
57	| Physics model change | Physics unit suite + truth-anchored tests at highest applicable L1-L4 |
58	| DB schema/ingestion change | Migration/schema edit + unit tests + integration/validation queries when cross-component |
59	| Report schema change | Producer + committed consumers + `docs/report_schemas/*` in same gate; no dual readers without tracked exit |
60	| Docs change | Reviewer check: correct repo/domain, valid commands, existing references, current workflow, `Last verified` when required |
61	| Compromise/exception | GitHub issue with reason, owner, and explicit exit condition |
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Architecture Boundaries
66	
67	Three verification/ownership regions:
68	
69	- **Data:** `src/data/`, `src/models/`, `src/common/`, `src/utils/`, `src/analysis/`, `src/simulation/`, `src/strategy/`, `src/reporting/`, `src/publishing/`
70	- **Physics:** `src/physics/`, `src/preprocessing/`
71	- **Evo:** `src/evo_predictor/`, `src/latent_power/`, `src/compound_prior/`
72	
73	Keep data, physics, and evo responsibilities distinct. Crossing boundaries requires explicit design decision and architecture/doc update. Do not plan shortcuts across regions without surfacing the tradeoff.
74	
75	Import posture follows the current architecture map and ADRs: data is the bottom layer; `latent_power` stays domain-independent; evo owns F1-specific adapters/orchestration; physics/preprocessing do not couple directly to evo.
76	
77	---
78

# F1Brainz — Orchestrator Context

**Project deltas over inherited global doctrine.** The approach baseline — rigorous-default posture,
map-first shaping, handoff completeness, gating, evidence, stop/ask — is inherited from the skills'
`references/global-orchestrator.md` + `references/global-everyone.md`. This file carries only F1Brainz
facts and the points where it departs.

---

## Project Identity

Personal F1 race prediction and fantasy strategy tool. Python + SQLite. Produces probabilistic race/ranking claims from historical session data. Developer + AI agents are the direct users; predictions influence real betting/fantasy decisions.

Not this: generic ML framework, live race-day data service, public API, or analysis layer that calls live FastF1/Jolpica.

**Output authority:**
- DB records: canonical; single source of truth
- Predictions: user-facing probabilistic claims; silent wrongness can cost money
- Promoted reports/manifests: canonical baseline until superseded
- Exploratory outputs/notebooks: non-canonical

**Failure modes to prevent:** silent wrong prediction, stale docs, hidden fallback, leakage, uncalibrated output, unreproducible result, untracked compromise, maintenance erosion.

**Operational reality:** output stakes are high, but operations are local/single-operator. No production deployment, staging, on-call, or test CI beyond docs checks. Verification evidence is local and human-reviewed.

---

## Canonical Data Constraint

The SQLite DB is the only authoritative source for analysis. No FastF1/Jolpica/live API calls from analysis, scorer, adapter, predictor, strategy, or backtest code. If the DB lacks needed data, plan an ingestion/schema change; do not patch analysis with a secondary source or silent fallback.

This is a planning gate for any work touching prediction inputs, adapters, scorers, backtests, reports, or strategy.

---

## Subsystem Rigor

| Subsystem | Rigor profile | Orchestrator implication |
|---|---|---|
| data layer | rigorous; schema and DB are authoritative | Plan ingestion/query validation; DB-only analysis is non-negotiable |
| evo_predictor / sampled runtime / strategy | rigorous; probabilistic claims need calibrated baselines | Require stable baseline, held-out backtest where material, Brier primary for gold comparison |
| latent_power / compound_prior | rigorous; solver/artifact contracts matter | Require explicit contracts, fixture/schema checks, no F1 leakage into generic solver |
| physics / preprocessing | rigorous; physical plausibility and numerics matter | Require truth-anchored L1-L4 evidence, units, bounds, invariants |
| committed report schemas/artifacts | rigorous; consumers depend on on-disk shape | Plan producer + committed consumer + schema doc updates atomically |
| exploratory notebooks/prototypes | pragmatic | Keep isolated; convert lessons into code/tests/metrics/docs before promotion |

---

## Evidence Requirements

| Change type | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Logic change on promoted path | Test-led; focused region suite green; no implementation-only logic commits |
| Python refactor / new modules in `src/` or `tests/` | `py -m src.utils.simplification_limits` on touched paths (strict); plan file splits when approaching limits |
| Architecture/boundary change | Region suite + architecture/doc update + deliberate approval |
| Evo/probability change | Evo unit suite + calibrated metric against stable baseline; Brier primary when comparing gold |
| Physics model change | Physics unit suite + truth-anchored tests at highest applicable L1-L4 |
| DB schema/ingestion change | Migration/schema edit + unit tests + integration/validation queries when cross-component |
| Report schema change | Producer + committed consumers + `docs/report_schemas/*` in same gate; no dual readers without tracked exit |
| Docs change | Reviewer check: correct repo/domain, valid commands, existing references, current workflow, `Last verified` when required |
| Compromise/exception | GitHub issue with reason, owner, and explicit exit condition |

---

## Architecture Boundaries

Three verification/ownership regions:

- **Data:** `src/data/`, `src/models/`, `src/common/`, `src/utils/`, `src/analysis/`, `src/simulation/`, `src/strategy/`, `src/reporting/`, `src/publishing/`
- **Physics:** `src/physics/`, `src/preprocessing/`
- **Evo:** `src/evo_predictor/`, `src/latent_power/`, `src/compound_prior/`

Keep data, physics, and evo responsibilities distinct. Crossing boundaries requires explicit design decision and architecture/doc update. Do not plan shortcuts across regions without surfacing the tradeoff.

Import posture follows the current architecture map and ADRs: data is the bottom layer; `latent_power` stays domain-independent; evo owns F1-specific adapters/orchestration; physics/preprocessing do not couple directly to evo.

---

## Planning Invariants

- Time-dependent prediction inputs require an as-of contract; silent "latest" fallback is not acceptable
- Missingness is explicit and configured, not guessed away at the DB boundary
- Tunable weights, thresholds, and heuristics belong in config or named constants; hidden inline tuning is review-risk
- Generated ML artifacts are derived; plan source/config/regeneration changes, not manual artifact edits
- Notebooks are scratch; convert useful lessons into code, tests, metrics, or docs
- Diagnose before fixing when the premise is uncertain: when an issue inherits a prior run's diagnosis or the fix locus is unclear, plan the first gate as an evidence-only diagnosis with a human decide-fix checkpoint before any code — let the evidence redirect the plan rather than coding the assumed fix
- Handoffs cite exact seams and their consumer topology: when reusing an existing seam (signature/return type, store table, config key, unit convention), cite the verified value from source AND who else consumes it and in what convention — a from-memory or single-consumer view causes rediscovery and missed blast radius

---

## Documentation Authority

Docs describe current truth, not archaeology. Each doc has one job: commands in command docs, durable rationale in agent context/ADRs, structure in architecture docs. (Updating docs when meaning changes is inherited; this names the F1Brainz placement.) Command-heavy docs need `Last verified` when `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` requires it.

---

## Repo Action Authority

| Action | Permission |
|---|---|
| Read files, inspect code, run tests | Autonomous |
| Create issues, comments, branches, worktrees | Autonomous for non-trivial tasks |
| Write/edit code or docs | Autonomous on task branch |
| Commit locally after verification passes | Autonomous |
| Push branches or open PRs | Ask first unless user explicitly asked to publish |
| Merge PRs | Ask first |
| Delete files | Ask first |
| Close or reopen issues | Ask first |
| Force-push to `main` / `master` | Forbidden; warn the user if asked |

---

## Compromise Policy

Any planned violation of project tenets requires a GitHub issue with reason, owner, and exit condition. Examples: non-DB analysis source, compatibility bridge, dual execution path, missing test seam, deferred stale doc, old report schema tolerance. Surface at planning time.

---

## Stop / Ask (project-specific, beyond the inherited triggers)

- Work crosses data/physics/evo boundaries without a prior design decision
- Current architecture truth is unclear enough that planning would be guesswork

16	| **compound prior** | Fitted tire-wear/compound artifact from `src/compound_prior/`; used for runtime lap-time normalization before evo features. Distinct from a tire **compound**. |

22	| **gate** | Verifiable increment with explicit success criteria and evidence. Do not advance until criteria are met. |
23	| **machine-checkable evidence** | Reusable proof such as tests, metrics, validation queries, schema checks, or captured command output. Not notebook impressions or visual spot checks. |
24	| **one canonical path** | Project doctrine: prefer one clear execution method over compatibility shims, aliases, dual formats, or fallback branches. Temporary exceptions require an issue with an exit condition. |
25	| **compromise (explicit)** | Known tenet violation tracked with a GitHub issue containing reason, owner, and exit condition. Required before introducing a compromise. |
26	| **missingness** | Intentional representation of absent data. Never guessed, zeroed, or silently substituted. |
27	| **time-dependent lookup** | Query/join/computation whose result depends on season, round, date, phase, or cutoff. Must state whether fallback is allowed. |
28	| **latent field / pi** | Event-local latent ordering scalar field inferred by latent_power. Higher pi ranks a driver/entity ahead for that event. |
29	| **race_power** | Event-specific latent race-ordering signal inferred from race-weekend evidence. Not engine or power-unit capability. |
30	| **PairBatch** | Validated directed-pair batch carrying antisymmetric features, data quality indicators, pair indices, and optional pairwise outcomes. Internal adapter/latent_power contract. |
31	| **latent field fusion** | Bayesian composition of module-local latent fields into the canonical field consumed by ranking/scoring, using precision weighting. |
32	| **retroactive_truth_power** | After-the-fact event-local latent field solved from observed phase outcome; used as supervision signal for missing predictive features. |
33	| **PhaseObservation** | Per-(event, phase) input to retroactive BT solver with pair outcomes, start-bias offsets, weights, and dropped-driver provenance. |
34	| **circuit entry (circuits.yaml)** | Per-year circuit configuration in `src/evo_predictor/circuits.yaml`. Exact year required; no silent fallback to prior year. |
35	| **form channel** | Recent-race performance signal fed into evo scoring. Configurable via `--form-lookback` and `--form-drop-worst`. |
36	| **DNF_POSITION** | Data-layer sentinel for did-not-finish/non-classified values where that legacy representation still applies. Not part of sampled-runtime/strategy exchange contracts. |
37	| **L1-L4 (physics tests)** | Truth levels for physics evidence: L1=analytical reference, L2=invariant/known-answer, L3=limit/degenerate case, L4=independent benchmark parity. |
38	| **canonical baseline** | Promoted artifact/config/report set that represents the current accepted performance reference. |
39	| **artifact policy** | Rules in `docs/artifact_policy.md` governing committed vs. excluded generated artifacts. |
40	| **report schema doc** | Contract under `docs/report_schemas/` for committed JSON/report shapes. Producers, consumers, and schema docs move together. |
41	| **`py`** | Windows Python Launcher command for this repo. Use `py`, not `python`. |

Curated, bounded workflow lessons for this repo — the distilled derivative of the

### lesson:crew-idle-strands-deliverable
- scope: constellation
- task-class: general-workflow
- statement: Long single detached completion-watchers (a bare Monitor wait, a lone background poller) get harness-reaped mid-run, silently killing the crew's own wake mechanism -- the crew then LOOKS idle/stalled with the deliverable unwritten, but the root cause is platform reaping, not the crew choosing to idle. Symptom recovery (commander nudges via SendMessage) still works, but the FIX is upstream of the symptom: use bounded chained waiters (each poll window under the reap threshold) or foreground in-turn polling instead of one long single waiter; verify liveness via PowerShell `Get-Process` CPU accumulation (NOT git-bash `ps`, which uses an unreliable PID shim); detach genuinely long jobs via `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden` (true OS-level detach) rather than `nohup ... &` inside a Bash tool call (still harness-tracked, still reapable). Handoffs/launch orders should mandate bounded/in-turn polling up front rather than relying on a nudge to recover after the fact.

### lesson:loo-residual-diagnostic-over-self-weighted-predictor
- scope: handoff
- task-class: physics-fitting
- statement: Any residual / calibration / stability diagnostic computed over a self-weighted or smoothing predictor (drift fit, RTS smoother, kernel) MUST use leave-one-out (out-of-sample) prediction. A self-inclusive form pins the prediction to each point's own value and is structurally blind to the very failure it exists to detect (sigma-too-small / over-claiming, between-session instability). When a crew flags this class once, sweep the whole module for sibling diagnostics rather than fixing only the flagged instance. Apply the same LOO discipline to the TARGET variable in a supplant/evaluation test: a truth channel derived from the same signal family as the feature, or algebraically collinear with it, yields spuriously high LOO P — gate with P>=0.95-means-leakage. Also verify the truth OLS is full-rank; within-stint fixed-effects + tyre_life are collinear (lap_number = offset + tyre_life within a stint), so use driver or race fixed-effects for the fuel term.

### lesson:crew-idle-strands-deliverable
- scope: constellation
- task-class: general-workflow
- statement: Long single detached completion-watchers (a bare Monitor wait, a lone background poller) get harness-reaped mid-run, silently killing the crew's own wake mechanism -- the crew then LOOKS idle/stalled with the deliverable unwritten, but the root cause is platform reaping, not the crew choosing to idle. Symptom recovery (commander nudges via SendMessage) still works, but the FIX is upstream of the symptom: use bounded chained waiters (each poll window under the reap threshold) or foreground in-turn polling instead of one long single waiter; verify liveness via PowerShell `Get-Process` CPU accumulation (NOT git-bash `ps`, which uses an unreliable PID shim); detach genuinely long jobs via `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden` (true OS-level detach) rather than `nohup ... &` inside a Bash tool call (still harness-tracked, still reapable). Handoffs/launch orders should mandate bounded/in-turn polling up front rather than relying on a nudge to recover after the fact.

### lesson:loo-residual-diagnostic-over-self-weighted-predictor
- scope: handoff
- task-class: physics-fitting
- statement: Any residual / calibration / stability diagnostic computed over a self-weighted or smoothing predictor (drift fit, RTS smoother, kernel) MUST use leave-one-out (out-of-sample) prediction. A self-inclusive form pins the prediction to each point's own value and is structurally blind to the very failure it exists to detect (sigma-too-small / over-claiming, between-session instability). When a crew flags this class once, sweep the whole module for sibling diagnostics rather than fixing only the flagged instance. Apply the same LOO discipline to the TARGET variable in a supplant/evaluation test: a truth channel derived from the same signal family as the feature, or algebraically collinear with it, yields spuriously high LOO P — gate with P>=0.95-means-leakage. Also verify the truth OLS is full-rank; within-stint fixed-effects + tyre_life are collinear (lap_number = offset + tyre_life within a stint), so use driver or race fixed-effects for the fuel term.
- grounding: .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md 2026-06-28 512: recurred 2x in one run — covariance-honesty zstd (commit 431f6374) then stability tau_resid (commit 0116ec93); both went from blind (over-claim zstd 0.026; tau_resid 0.0000 on every axis) to detecting (1.98 / 0.71) only after switching to a shared leave-one-out _loo_drift_preds helper.

148:### lesson:admiral-owns-long-batch-compute
151:- statement: Multi-hour batch compute must be Admiral-owned and OS-detached (e.g. PowerShell Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden, which survives all three fleet-doctrine kill vectors). A commander's harness-tracked background workers die when the subagent idles -- guaranteed strand. Pattern: Admiral launches detached workers, records PIDs + state note, uses a durable watcher (Wait-Process) rather than a harness-tracked background; CLIs must be idempotent/resumable so partial runs continue. A commander may discover or diagnose batch scope, but must not be the one running multi-hour compute. When a Commander's OWN plan (not launch-order-mandated) folds a full-repo/full-suite regression check into a gate's closing postcondition, size it BEFORE freezing: grep the real import graph of changed files and scope to actual importers. Factor any standing thread-cap guard into runtime estimates. When launching a detached process with a multi-word argument, prefer the script's own in-code default/tuple over PowerShell's Start-Process -ArgumentList where possible. WHEN ARMING A STALL-WATCHDOG AGAINST A FILE'S MTIME, SNAPSHOT THAT MTIME AT ARM TIME -- do not key liveness off a pre-existing file's already-stale absolute age, or a healthy in-flight process will read as a false 'SILENT' alarm.
165:### lesson:scope-self-authored-regression-to-import-graph
168:- statement: When a Commander's OWN plan (not a launch-order-mandated check) folds a full-repo/full-suite regression command into a gate's closing postcondition, grep the actual import graph of the changed files FIRST and consider scoping the check to real importers -- a blanket 'run everything' check on a numerics-heavy suite can take 60-90+ minutes and get reaped by the harness before completion, forcing an emergency float-and-waive at the worst possible time (finalization). A targeted subset covering every actual importer is both faster and arguably more correctly scoped to the real risk surface.
180:### lesson:no-broad-process-kill-in-multiship-session
183:- statement: In a multi-ship/fleet session, NEVER broad-kill processes (e.g. `taskkill //IM python.exe`) — it kills sibling ships' compute. Kill by explicit PID, and check `ps -W` start-time/ownership before any sweep; treat clustered same-timestamp processes you didn't launch as a sibling's.
194:### lesson:delegated-commander-foreground-poll-over-watcher-yield
197:- statement: In a headless/delegated run, arming a fire-and-forget BACKGROUND watcher and ending the turn to 'wait' reads to the Admiral as IDLE and stalls the run between steps. 223:### lesson:idle-artifact-completeness-distinguisher
226:- statement: A commander idle_notification does not distinguish done from stalled. Before classifying idle+uncommitted as a stall, check crew-runs.json for active crew agents -- idle + uncommitted is NOT a stall if a crew is actively running for that work-id. Recovery for a stall = SendMessage return-and-continue with the same agent; do NOT kill and relaunch (idle/available means context is intact; two-agents-in-worktree risk otherwise). When a commander pattern-recurrently stalls at the push/PR/archive step across multiple nudge attempts, the Admiral should plan to own those closeout mechanics directly. 238:### lesson:false-stall-diagnosis
241:- statement: A background job that LOOKS stalled (idle notification, no fresh output, no obvious progress) may actually be healthy-but-slow or already-finished-but-sleeping -- check the signal that actually distinguishes those states before concluding a stall: (a) for a resumable batch, distinguish valid rows from error/smoke-leftover rows and confirm CPU is climbing (PowerShell `Get-Process`, not git-bash `ps`) rather than reading raw row-count alone; (b) for a claimed-complete deliverable, verify the process that was supposed to produce it actually ran to a real terminus (a captured verdict or traceback) -- code committed after a gated step reports 'stalled at start' with no live process means the work is UNRUN, not silently finished, regardless of what the commit timestamp implies.

255:- statement: A cartographer/architecture-map reconcile authored against a PR's ORIGINAL base commit goes stale if the PR later takes post-review expansion commits -- the reconcile documents a state the eventual merge no longer matches. 269:- statement: A SendMessage to a delegated commander/implementer queues until that agent's own turn boundary -- it is not delivered instantly. 298:### lesson:cartographer-subagent-wrong-checkout-root
301:- statement: A Cartographer subagent dispatched at the reconcile step, given the worktree's absolute path in its dispatch prompt, wrote all its architecture-doc edits (docs/architecture/packets/*.md, index.md, overlays/*.yml, a new decisions/*.md file) to the MAIN CHECKOUT instead of the assigned worktree -- a git-invisible failure caught only because the dispatching commander independently ran git status in BOTH locations. 316:- statement: When a gate's plan ADDS to a previously-ratified/frozen/consumed module, its acceptance criteria MUST explicitly include re-running that module's OWN pre-existing test file(s), not just the newly authored tests for the new content. 343:### lesson:season-batch-runner-per-round-fault-isolation
346:- statement: A real-data multi-round/multi-item batch runner over the epic-659 pipeline MUST isolate per-item failures (try/except-per-item -> PARK with a diagnosis + continue), never let one item's exception kill the whole batch. 361:- statement: A subagent's (crew, cartographer, or Commander's) own claim of having done/verified/reapplied something is not reliable ground truth on its own, and a green mechanical check (e.g. check_arch_map) can be structurally blind to content drift by construction. 376:- statement: Multiple constellation-commander scripts assume a work_id has no internal '/', breaking under this repo's own nested Commander-under-Admiral convention (epic-<N>/<issue>, e.g. epic-659/665). 1	"""Per-driver, per-CLASS utilization observable (issue #664, epic #659, g3).
2	
3	Composes three things over a frozen :class:`~src.physics.segment_map.runtime.SegmentMap`
4	and a driver's real qualifying lap against their constructor's ``strictly_pre=True``
5	ideal-lap ceiling, all on a SHARED distance grid:
6	
7	    1. **Point deficit** — the g1 ``class_ledger.class_deficits`` per-CLASS ABSOLUTE
8	       speed (m/s) AND transit-time (s) deficit. This is the load-bearing anti-circular
9	       (#628) quantity: ``mean(v_ideal - v_real)`` and ``Δt_real - Δt_ideal`` — never a
10	       ratio. It is what module G must NOT change (see below).
11	    2. **One-sided grip (G) uncertainty band** — a σ⁺-only, heavy-tailed (Student-t)
12	       band wrapping the per-class TIME deficit. See the binding pre-ruling below.
13	    3. **Relative energy-deployment channel** — a descriptive/instrument proxy. See the
14	       ENERGY elevation-convention finding below.
15	
16	This is a smoother-agnostic PURE NUMERIC core: no DB / session / FastF1 / store I/O
17	(the live end-to-end that loads a session and fetches G from the grip store is g4).
18	
19	Binding pre-ruling — G is a ONE-SIDED directed uncertainty, NOT a point subtraction
20	------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
21	Module G (:func:`src.physics.layer2.grip_store.get_grip_at`) is consumed as a
22	``(μ=0, σ⁺-only)`` half/truncated Student-t on the "grip only improves" side:
23	
24	* The utilization POINT deficit is **UNCHANGED** by G — this module NEVER subtracts a
25	  point G, NEVER re-fits G, and NEVER moves G's μ off zero (sharpening μ is #678, out of
26	  scope). ``point_deficit`` is byte-identical with and without the G wrap.
27	* G is consumed via ``get_grip_at`` returning ``(mu, sigma)``. Its magnitude/σ becomes
28	  the **SCALE** of a one-sided band, not a shift: :func:`onesided_sigma_from_grip`
29	  computes ``σ⁺ = hypot(mu, sigma) ≥ 0``. The band extends ONLY toward LARGER deficit
30	  (grip could have flattered the real lap, so the true skill-deficit could be larger).
31	* "G barely moves utilization" is the CORRECT, expected first-pass outcome — the band is
32	  a directed uncertainty envelope, not a point correction.
33	
34	The band is a HALF/truncated Student-t built from :mod:`src.common.student_t`
35	(``PredictiveT`` at ``DEFAULT_NU_LOSS``) — heavy-tailed, NO baked-in normality.
36	
37	Legacy pre-#627 grip rows expose a narrower/absent ``curve_*_sigma`` and therefore a
38	smaller σ⁺ (a narrower band); this SOFT-DEGRADES (a narrower honest width), it never
39	crashes — a noted, non-blocking degrade per the launch order.
40	
41	ENERGY elevation-convention finding (STATED FIRST, decides single-vs-dual channel)
42	----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
43	**Finding: a SINGLE kinetic-energy (½v²) channel suffices; the total-mechanical-energy
44	(½v² + g·h) convention is NOT needed here.** Reasoning: the deployment proxy is
45	explicitly RELATIVE — it compares deployment on the SAME circuit, referenced to the
46	car's own rolling baseline (and, at matched distance, the real lap against its own
47	ideal). The potential-energy term ``g·h(distance)`` is a property of the TRACK, identical
48	at each distance for both laps under comparison; and the proxy reads only KE *changes*
49	(``d(½v²)``, a derivative) — an absolute additive energy-level offset (an ERS/SOC
50	baseline) differentiates to zero, and the common-mode ``g·h`` cancels under the
51	same-circuit relative comparison. Total-mechanical-energy would only be required for an
52	ABSOLUTE, cross-circuit deployment figure — which is explicitly out of scope
53	(relative-not-absolute; there is no ERS/SOC channel in the telemetry, so an absolute
54	figure would be fabricated). Hence a single KE-based relative-deployment channel, with no
55	elevation input.
56	
57	The energy channel is **DESCRIPTIVE / instrument this run** — it is NOT gated by the g4
58	jackknife (its pre-registered comparison is downstream). Its honest proxy scope: a
59	relative share of positive (deployment/throttle-on) KE-gain per class plus the deployment
60	phase fraction, referenced to the car's own lap total. It does NOT read absolute SOC/kW.
61	A thresholded "derate flag" would mint a new physical threshold (out of scope) and is
62	therefore left as a present-but-dormant store column, not computed here.
63	
64	References: decision:c1_driver_utilization_design,
65	decision:class-attribution-membership-faithful, issue #664, epic #659; G one-sided wrap
66	(settled/inherited), #678 (μ-sharpening, out of scope), #628 (anti-circularity).
67	"""
68	from __future__ import annotations
69	
70	import math
71	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
72	from typing import Optional
73	
74	import numpy as np
75	
76	from src.common.student_t import DEFAULT_NU_LOSS, PredictiveT
77	from src.physics.layer2.grip_store import GripStore, get_grip_at
78	from src.physics.segment_map.runtime import SegmentMap
79	from src.physics.utilization.class_ledger import (
80	    ClassDeficits,
81	    DEFAULT_MIN_SPEED_MS,
82	    build_weight_matrix,
83	    class_deficits,
84	)
85	
86	__all__ = [
87	    "OneSidedGripBand",
88	    "onesided_sigma_from_grip",
89	    "grip_band",
90	    "grip_scale_from_store",
91	    "ClassEnergyChannel",
92	    "class_energy_channel",
93	    "energy_channel_from_specific_energy",
94	    "ClassUtilizationObservable",
95	    "compute_class_utilization_observable",
96	]

98	
99	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	# One-sided grip (G) uncertainty band — μ=0, σ⁺ only, half/truncated Student-t
101	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
102	
103	
104	def onesided_sigma_from_grip(mu: float, sigma: float) -> float:
105	    """The one-sided σ⁺ SCALE from module-G's ``(mu, sigma)`` — ``hypot(mu, sigma) ≥ 0``.
106	
107	    This is the WRAP POINT of the binding pre-ruling: G exposes only a point ``mu`` and
108	    its propagated ``sigma`` (``get_grip_at``); here BOTH become the *scale* of a
109	    one-sided band, NEVER a point shift. The RMS combination ``sqrt(mu² + sigma²)`` reads
110	    as "the total plausible magnitude of grip flattery" — the directed grip level ``mu``
111	    (how much grip could have flattered the real lap at this track-evolution point)
112	    combined in quadrature with its own uncertainty ``sigma``. It is:
113	
114	    * always ``≥ 0`` (a valid one-sided scale);
115	    * insensitive to the SIGN of ``mu`` (magnitude, not a signed shift — grip only
116	      improves, so the band direction is fixed by construction, not by ``mu``'s sign);
117	    * ``0`` only in the degenerate ``mu = sigma = 0`` case (no band).
118	
119	    ``mu`` is NEVER applied as a shift to the point deficit — sharpening the band's centre
120	    off zero is #678 (out of scope).
121	    """
122	    return float(math.hypot(float(mu), float(sigma)))
123	
124	
125	@dataclass(frozen=True)
126	class OneSidedGripBand:
127	    """A one-sided, heavy-tailed (Student-t) grip-uncertainty band on a point deficit.
128	
129	    The band's *centre* is the ABSOLUTE point deficit (``point_deficit``), UNCHANGED by G.
130	    G contributes ONLY ``sigma_plus`` (``≥ 0``), the scale of a HALF/truncated Student-t
131	    that extends solely toward LARGER deficit (grip could have flattered the real lap, so
132	    the true skill-deficit could be larger). The lower edge is the point itself — the band
133	    never reaches toward a smaller deficit.
134	
135	    ``nu`` is the project aleatoric loss dof (:data:`~src.common.student_t.DEFAULT_NU_LOSS`)
136	    — heavy-tailed, no baked-in normality.
137	    """
138	
139	    point_deficit: float
140	    sigma_plus: float
141	    nu: float = DEFAULT_NU_LOSS
142	
143	    def upper_bound(self, level: float) -> float:
144	        """One-sided upper credible bound at ``level`` (the ``level``-quantile of |T|).
145	
146	        For a folded (half) Student-t of scale ``sigma_plus``, the ``level``-quantile of
147	        the absolute deviation is ``t.ppf((1+level)/2, nu)`` — always ``> 0`` for
148	        ``level > 0`` — so the bound lies strictly ABOVE ``point_deficit`` whenever
149	        ``sigma_plus > 0``. A zero scale collapses the bound to the point.
150	        """
151	        if self.sigma_plus <= 0.0:
152	            return self.point_deficit
153	        pt = PredictiveT(nu=self.nu, loc=0.0, scale=self.sigma_plus)
154	        return self.point_deficit + pt.ppf(0.5 + 0.5 * float(level))

156	    def as_predictive_t(self) -> Optional[PredictiveT]:
157	        """The underlying (un-folded) Student-t located at the point deficit, or ``None``
158	        for a degenerate zero-scale band (``PredictiveT`` requires a positive scale)."""
159	        if self.sigma_plus <= 0.0:
160	            return None
161	        return PredictiveT(nu=self.nu, loc=self.point_deficit, scale=self.sigma_plus)

203	    the proxy reads only energy *changes*, an absolute additive energy-level offset
204	    cancels; the per-class share is normalised by the car's OWN lap deployment total (its

212	        Share of the lap's total positive (throttle-on) KE-gain attributed to each class,

231	    used here (kinetic; no ``g·h`` term, per the elevation-convention finding)."""

236	def energy_channel_from_specific_energy(
237	    segment_map: SegmentMap,
238	    distance_m: np.ndarray,

240	) -> ClassEnergyChannel:

242	
243	    Reads only the CHANGES ``d(specific_energy)`` between consecutive samples: the
244	    positive part is deployment (throttle-on KE gain), attributed to the segment of the
245	    interval's START sample and reduced to classes through the g1 attribution matrix
246	    ``W``. Because only *changes* are read, an absolute additive offset to
247	    ``specific_energy`` (a fictitious SOC/kW baseline) leaves every output unchanged — the
248	    load-bearing relative-not-absolute property.
249	    """
250	    distance_m = np.asarray(distance_m, dtype=np.float64)
251	    specific_energy = np.asarray(specific_energy, dtype=np.float64)
252	    if len(specific_energy) != len(distance_m):
253	        raise ValueError(
254	            f"specific_energy: expected length {len(distance_m)} (same as distance_m), "
255	            f"got {len(specific_energy)}"
256	        )
257	
258	    de = np.diff(specific_energy)
259	    deployment = np.clip(de, 0.0, None)  # positive KE gain only (throttle-on)
260	
261	    seg_of_interval = segment_map.segment_of(distance_m[:-1])
262	    dep_seg = np.zeros(segment_map.n_segments, dtype=np.float64)
263	    np.add.at(dep_seg, seg_of_interval, deployment)
264	
265	    W, class_ids = build_weight_matrix(segment_map)
266	    dep_by_class = W.T @ dep_seg
267	    total = float(dep_by_class.sum())
268	
269	    share = np.full(W.shape[1], np.nan, dtype=np.float64)
270	    if total > 0.0:
271	        share = dep_by_class / total
272	
273	    ds = np.diff(distance_m)
274	    deploy_dist = float(ds[de > 0.0].sum())
275	    phase_fraction = deploy_dist / float(ds.sum())
276	
277	    return ClassEnergyChannel(
278	        class_ids=class_ids,
279	        deployment_share_by_class=share,
280	        deployment_phase_fraction=phase_fraction,

282	    )

325	        band. ``0.0`` when no grip signal was supplied — G then adds no width, and the
326	        point deficits are exactly the no-G values (the correct, expected outcome).
327	    bands:
328	        Per-class :class:`OneSidedGripBand`, in ``class_ids`` order. Each band is centred
329	        on that class's (unshifted) TIME deficit and carries the shared
330	        :attr:`g_sigma_onesided` scale — a one-sided, heavy-tailed uncertainty envelope,

332	    """

335	    speed_deficit_by_class: np.ndarray
336	    time_deficit_by_class: np.ndarray
337	    n_points_by_class: np.ndarray

351	    distance_m: np.ndarray,
352	    v_ideal: np.ndarray,
353	    v_real: np.ndarray,
354	    *,
355	    grip: Optional[tuple[float, float]] = None,
356	    min_speed_ms: float = DEFAULT_MIN_SPEED_MS,
357	) -> ClassUtilizationObservable:
358	    """Build the per-class utilization observable for one real-vs-ideal lap pair.
359	
360	    ``distance_m`` (m, strictly increasing) carries ``v_ideal`` (the constructor's
361	    ``strictly_pre=True`` ideal-lap ceiling) and ``v_real`` (the driver's real lap) on
362	    the SAME grid — exactly the g1 ``class_deficits`` contract (resample upstream if the
363	    real lap and the ribbon differ in length; this pure core does not reinvent a

"""Per-driver, per-CLASS utilization observable (issue #664, epic #659, g3).

Composes three things over a frozen :class:`~src.physics.segment_map.runtime.SegmentMap`
and a driver's real qualifying lap against their constructor's ``strictly_pre=True``
ideal-lap ceiling, all on a SHARED distance grid:

    1. **Point deficit** — the g1 ``class_ledger.class_deficits`` per-CLASS ABSOLUTE
       speed (m/s) AND transit-time (s) deficit. This is the load-bearing anti-circular
       (#628) quantity: ``mean(v_ideal - v_real)`` and ``Δt_real - Δt_ideal`` — never a
       ratio. It is what module G must NOT change (see below).
    2. **One-sided grip (G) uncertainty band** — a σ⁺-only, heavy-tailed (Student-t)
       band wrapping the per-class TIME deficit. See the binding pre-ruling below.
    3. **Relative energy-deployment channel** — a descriptive/instrument proxy. See the
       ENERGY elevation-convention finding below.

This is a smoother-agnostic PURE NUMERIC core: no DB / session / FastF1 / store I/O
(the live end-to-end that loads a session and fetches G from the grip store is g4).

Binding pre-ruling — G is a ONE-SIDED directed uncertainty, NOT a point subtraction
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Module G (:func:`src.physics.layer2.grip_store.get_grip_at`) is consumed as a
``(μ=0, σ⁺-only)`` half/truncated Student-t on the "grip only improves" side:

* The utilization POINT deficit is **UNCHANGED** by G — this module NEVER subtracts a
  point G, NEVER re-fits G, and NEVER moves G's μ off zero (sharpening μ is #678, out of
  scope). ``point_deficit`` is byte-identical with and without the G wrap.
* G is consumed via ``get_grip_at`` returning ``(mu, sigma)``. Its magnitude/σ becomes
  the **SCALE** of a one-sided band, not a shift: :func:`onesided_sigma_from_grip`
  computes ``σ⁺ = hypot(mu, sigma) ≥ 0``. The band extends ONLY toward LARGER deficit
  (grip could have flattered the real lap, so the true skill-deficit could be larger).
* "G barely moves utilization" is the CORRECT, expected first-pass outcome — the band is
  a directed uncertainty envelope, not a point correction.

The band is a HALF/truncated Student-t built from :mod:`src.common.student_t`
(``PredictiveT`` at ``DEFAULT_NU_LOSS``) — heavy-tailed, NO baked-in normality.

Legacy pre-#627 grip rows expose a narrower/absent ``curve_*_sigma`` and therefore a
smaller σ⁺ (a narrower band); this SOFT-DEGRADES (a narrower honest width), it never
crashes — a noted, non-blocking degrade per the launch order.

ENERGY elevation-convention finding (STATED FIRST, decides single-vs-dual channel)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
**Finding: a SINGLE kinetic-energy (½v²) channel suffices; the total-mechanical-energy
(½v² + g·h) convention is NOT needed here.** Reasoning: the deployment proxy is
explicitly RELATIVE — it compares deployment on the SAME circuit, referenced to the
car's own rolling baseline (and, at matched distance, the real lap against its own
ideal). The potential-energy term ``g·h(distance)`` is a property of the TRACK, identical
at each distance for both laps under comparison; and the proxy reads only KE *changes*
(``d(½v²)``, a derivative) — an absolute additive energy-level offset (an ERS/SOC
baseline) differentiates to zero, and the common-mode ``g·h`` cancels under the
same-circuit relative comparison. Total-mechanical-energy would only be required for an
ABSOLUTE, cross-circuit deployment figure — which is explicitly out of scope
(relative-not-absolute; there is no ERS/SOC channel in the telemetry, so an absolute
figure would be fabricated). Hence a single KE-based relative-deployment channel, with no
elevation input.

The energy channel is **DESCRIPTIVE / instrument this run** — it is NOT gated by the g4
jackknife (its pre-registered comparison is downstream). Its honest proxy scope: a
relative share of positive (deployment/throttle-on) KE-gain per class plus the deployment
phase fraction, referenced to the car's own lap total. It does NOT read absolute SOC/kW.
A thresholded "derate flag" would mint a new physical threshold (out of scope) and is
therefore left as a present-but-dormant store column, not computed here.

References: decision:c1_driver_utilization_design,
decision:class-attribution-membership-faithful, issue #664, epic #659; G one-sided wrap
(settled/inherited), #678 (μ-sharpening, out of scope), #628 (anti-circularity).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Optional

import numpy as np

from src.common.student_t import DEFAULT_NU_LOSS, PredictiveT
from src.physics.layer2.grip_store import GripStore, get_grip_at
from src.physics.segment_map.runtime import SegmentMap
from src.physics.utilization.class_ledger import (
    ClassDeficits,
    DEFAULT_MIN_SPEED_MS,
    build_weight_matrix,
    class_deficits,
)

__all__ = [
    "OneSidedGripBand",
    "onesided_sigma_from_grip",
    "grip_band",
    "grip_scale_from_store",
    "ClassEnergyChannel",
    "class_energy_channel",
    "energy_channel_from_specific_energy",
    "ClassUtilizationObservable",
    "compute_class_utilization_observable",
]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One-sided grip (G) uncertainty band — μ=0, σ⁺ only, half/truncated Student-t
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def onesided_sigma_from_grip(mu: float, sigma: float) -> float:
    """The one-sided σ⁺ SCALE from module-G's ``(mu, sigma)`` — ``hypot(mu, sigma) ≥ 0``.

    This is the WRAP POINT of the binding pre-ruling: G exposes only a point ``mu`` and
    its propagated ``sigma`` (``get_grip_at``); here BOTH become the *scale* of a
    one-sided band, NEVER a point shift. The RMS combination ``sqrt(mu² + sigma²)`` reads
    as "the total plausible magnitude of grip flattery" — the directed grip level ``mu``
    (how much grip could have flattered the real lap at this track-evolution point)
    combined in quadrature with its own uncertainty ``sigma``. It is:

    * always ``≥ 0`` (a valid one-sided scale);
    * insensitive to the SIGN of ``mu`` (magnitude, not a signed shift — grip only
      improves, so the band direction is fixed by construction, not by ``mu``'s sign);
    * ``0`` only in the degenerate ``mu = sigma = 0`` case (no band).

    ``mu`` is NEVER applied as a shift to the point deficit — sharpening the band's centre
    off zero is #678 (out of scope).
    """
    return float(math.hypot(float(mu), float(sigma)))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OneSidedGripBand:
    """A one-sided, heavy-tailed (Student-t) grip-uncertainty band on a point deficit.

    The band's *centre* is the ABSOLUTE point deficit (``point_deficit``), UNCHANGED by G.
    G contributes ONLY ``sigma_plus`` (``≥ 0``), the scale of a HALF/truncated Student-t
    that extends solely toward LARGER deficit (grip could have flattered the real lap, so
    the true skill-deficit could be larger). The lower edge is the point itself — the band
    never reaches toward a smaller deficit.

    ``nu`` is the project aleatoric loss dof (:data:`~src.common.student_t.DEFAULT_NU_LOSS`)
    — heavy-tailed, no baked-in normality.
    """

    point_deficit: float
    sigma_plus: float
    nu: float = DEFAULT_NU_LOSS

    def upper_bound(self, level: float) -> float:
        """One-sided upper credible bound at ``level`` (the ``level``-quantile of |T|).

        For a folded (half) Student-t of scale ``sigma_plus``, the ``level``-quantile of
        the absolute deviation is ``t.ppf((1+level)/2, nu)`` — always ``> 0`` for
        ``level > 0`` — so the bound lies strictly ABOVE ``point_deficit`` whenever
        ``sigma_plus > 0``. A zero scale collapses the bound to the point.
        """
        if self.sigma_plus <= 0.0:
            return self.point_deficit
        pt = PredictiveT(nu=self.nu, loc=0.0, scale=self.sigma_plus)
        return self.point_deficit + pt.ppf(0.5 + 0.5 * float(level))

    def as_predictive_t(self) -> Optional[PredictiveT]:
        """The underlying (un-folded) Student-t located at the point deficit, or ``None``
        for a degenerate zero-scale band (``PredictiveT`` requires a positive scale)."""
        if self.sigma_plus <= 0.0:
            return None
        return PredictiveT(nu=self.nu, loc=self.point_deficit, scale=self.sigma_plus)


def grip_band(
    point_deficit: float, sigma_plus: float, *, nu: float = DEFAULT_NU_LOSS
) -> OneSidedGripBand:
    """Construct a :class:`OneSidedGripBand` (validates ``sigma_plus ≥ 0``)."""
    if not math.isfinite(sigma_plus) or sigma_plus < 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"sigma_plus must be finite and >= 0 (one-sided), got {sigma_plus}")
    return OneSidedGripBand(
        point_deficit=float(point_deficit), sigma_plus=float(sigma_plus), nu=float(nu)
    )


def grip_scale_from_store(
    store: GripStore,
    year: int,
    gp_name: str,
    session_type: str,
    cumulative_track_laps: int,
) -> float:
    """CONSUME module G via ``get_grip_at`` and return the one-sided σ⁺ scale.

    The single seam a caller (g4) uses to turn the stored grip curve into this module's
    band scale. G is CONSUMED (``get_grip_at`` -> ``(mu, sigma)``), never re-fit; the
    ``(mu, sigma)`` is wrapped by :func:`onesided_sigma_from_grip`.
    """
    mu, sigma = get_grip_at(store, year, gp_name, session_type, cumulative_track_laps)
    return onesided_sigma_from_grip(mu, sigma)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Energy channel — RELATIVE deployment proxy (single KE channel; see finding above)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClassEnergyChannel:
    """RELATIVE energy-deployment proxy per class for one lap (DESCRIPTIVE / instrument).

    Built from KINETIC-energy *changes* only (``d(½v²)``) — never an absolute SOC/kW
    level (there is no ERS/SOC channel; an absolute figure would be fabricated). Because
    the proxy reads only energy *changes*, an absolute additive energy-level offset
    cancels; the per-class share is normalised by the car's OWN lap deployment total (its
    rolling baseline), so the channel is relative in both senses.

    Attributes
    ----------
    class_ids:
        The ``(2+k)`` class vocabulary in ``W``-column order.
    deployment_share_by_class:
        Share of the lap's total positive (throttle-on) KE-gain attributed to each class,
        ``(Wᵀ deployment_seg) / Σ deployment`` — a RELATIVE fraction summing to 1 over
        populated classes. ``nan`` for every class when the lap has no deployment.
    deployment_phase_fraction:
        Fraction of lap DISTANCE spent in a deployment (positive-KE-gain) phase — a coarse
        phase-structure descriptor in ``[0, 1]``.
    total_deployment_energy:
        The car's own lap deployment total ``Σ max(d(½v²), 0)`` (specific, J/kg) — the
        rolling baseline the shares are relative to. Diagnostic only.
    """

    class_ids: tuple[str, ...]
    deployment_share_by_class: np.ndarray
    deployment_phase_fraction: float
    total_deployment_energy: float


def _specific_kinetic_energy(speed: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Specific kinetic energy ``½v²`` (J/kg) per sample — the ONLY energy convention
    used here (kinetic; no ``g·h`` term, per the elevation-convention finding)."""
    speed = np.asarray(speed, dtype=np.float64)
    return 0.5 * speed * speed


def energy_channel_from_specific_energy(
    segment_map: SegmentMap,
    distance_m: np.ndarray,
    specific_energy: np.ndarray,
) -> ClassEnergyChannel:
    """Build the :class:`ClassEnergyChannel` from a per-sample specific-energy profile.

    Reads only the CHANGES ``d(specific_energy)`` between consecutive samples: the
    positive part is deployment (throttle-on KE gain), attributed to the segment of the
    interval's START sample and reduced to classes through the g1 attribution matrix
    ``W``. Because only *changes* are read, an absolute additive offset to
    ``specific_energy`` (a fictitious SOC/kW baseline) leaves every output unchanged — the
    load-bearing relative-not-absolute property.
    """
    distance_m = np.asarray(distance_m, dtype=np.float64)
    specific_energy = np.asarray(specific_energy, dtype=np.float64)
    if len(specific_energy) != len(distance_m):
        raise ValueError(
            f"specific_energy: expected length {len(distance_m)} (same as distance_m), "
            f"got {len(specific_energy)}"
        )

    de = np.diff(specific_energy)
    deployment = np.clip(de, 0.0, None)  # positive KE gain only (throttle-on)

    seg_of_interval = segment_map.segment_of(distance_m[:-1])
    dep_seg = np.zeros(segment_map.n_segments, dtype=np.float64)
    np.add.at(dep_seg, seg_of_interval, deployment)

    W, class_ids = build_weight_matrix(segment_map)
    dep_by_class = W.T @ dep_seg
    total = float(dep_by_class.sum())

    share = np.full(W.shape[1], np.nan, dtype=np.float64)
    if total > 0.0:
        share = dep_by_class / total

    ds = np.diff(distance_m)
    deploy_dist = float(ds[de > 0.0].sum())
    phase_fraction = deploy_dist / float(ds.sum())

    return ClassEnergyChannel(
        class_ids=class_ids,
        deployment_share_by_class=share,
        deployment_phase_fraction=phase_fraction,
        total_deployment_energy=total,
    )


def class_energy_channel(
    segment_map: SegmentMap,
    distance_m: np.ndarray,
    speed: np.ndarray,
) -> ClassEnergyChannel:
    """RELATIVE deployment channel from a lap's ``(distance_m, speed)`` profile.

    Thin convenience: converts ``speed`` to specific kinetic energy ``½v²`` and delegates
    to :func:`energy_channel_from_specific_energy`.
    """
    return energy_channel_from_specific_energy(
        segment_map, distance_m, _specific_kinetic_energy(speed)
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Observable result
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClassUtilizationObservable:
    """Per-driver, per-CLASS utilization observable over one weekend lap-pair.

    Attributes
    ----------
    class_ids:
        The ``(2+k)`` class vocabulary in ``W``-column order (from g1).
    speed_deficit_by_class:
        g1 ABSOLUTE mean speed deficit ``mean(v_ideal - v_real)`` (m/s) per class.
        ``nan`` for an unpopulated class. UNCHANGED by G.
    time_deficit_by_class:
        g1 ABSOLUTE transit-time deficit ``Δt_real - Δt_ideal`` (s) per class — the
        location of each per-class one-sided grip band. UNCHANGED by G.
    n_points_by_class:
        Soft-membership-weighted sample count backing each class (from g1).
    lap_time_deficit_s:
        Whole-lap transit-time deficit (s); positive = real slower than ideal.
    g_sigma_onesided:
        The session-level one-sided grip σ⁺ scale (``≥ 0``) applied to every per-class
        band. ``0.0`` when no grip signal was supplied — G then adds no width, and the
        point deficits are exactly the no-G values (the correct, expected outcome).
    bands:
        Per-class :class:`OneSidedGripBand`, in ``class_ids`` order. Each band is centred
        on that class's (unshifted) TIME deficit and carries the shared
        :attr:`g_sigma_onesided` scale — a one-sided, heavy-tailed uncertainty envelope,
        NOT a point correction.
    """

    class_ids: tuple[str, ...]
    speed_deficit_by_class: np.ndarray
    time_deficit_by_class: np.ndarray
    n_points_by_class: np.ndarray
    lap_time_deficit_s: float
    g_sigma_onesided: float = 0.0
    bands: tuple[OneSidedGripBand, ...] = field(default_factory=tuple)
    energy: Optional[ClassEnergyChannel] = None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Observable core
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def compute_class_utilization_observable(
    segment_map: SegmentMap,
    distance_m: np.ndarray,
    v_ideal: np.ndarray,
    v_real: np.ndarray,
    *,
    grip: Optional[tuple[float, float]] = None,
    min_speed_ms: float = DEFAULT_MIN_SPEED_MS,
) -> ClassUtilizationObservable:
    """Build the per-class utilization observable for one real-vs-ideal lap pair.

    ``distance_m`` (m, strictly increasing) carries ``v_ideal`` (the constructor's
    ``strictly_pre=True`` ideal-lap ceiling) and ``v_real`` (the driver's real lap) on
    the SAME grid — exactly the g1 ``class_deficits`` contract (resample upstream if the
    real lap and the ribbon differ in length; this pure core does not reinvent a
    resampler).

    ``grip`` is the ``(mu, sigma)`` pair from :func:`~src.physics.layer2.grip_store.get_grip_at`
    (fetched by the caller — this pure core takes it as data, so it stays unit-testable
    without a live store). It is consumed ONLY as a one-sided σ⁺ SCALE
    (:func:`onesided_sigma_from_grip`); it NEVER shifts the point deficit. When ``grip`` is
    ``None`` the σ⁺ is ``0`` and the point deficits are returned exactly.

    The returned point deficits are the g1 ``class_deficits`` values verbatim — ABSOLUTE,
    anti-circular, never a ratio, and identical whether or not ``grip`` is supplied.
    """
    deficits: ClassDeficits = class_deficits(
        segment_map, distance_m, v_ideal, v_real, min_speed_ms=min_speed_ms
    )

    g_sigma_onesided = (
        0.0 if grip is None else onesided_sigma_from_grip(grip[0], grip[1])
    )
    bands = tuple(
        grip_band(point_deficit=float(td), sigma_plus=g_sigma_onesided)
        for td in deficits.time_deficit_by_class
    )

    # RELATIVE deployment channel over the driver's REAL lap (descriptive/instrument).
    energy = class_energy_channel(segment_map, distance_m, v_real)

    return ClassUtilizationObservable(
        class_ids=deficits.class_ids,
        speed_deficit_by_class=deficits.speed_deficit_by_class,
        time_deficit_by_class=deficits.time_deficit_by_class,
        n_points_by_class=deficits.n_points_by_class,
        lap_time_deficit_s=deficits.lap_time_deficit_s,
        g_sigma_onesided=g_sigma_onesided,
        bands=bands,
        energy=energy,
    )

{"body":"## Defect

`onesided_sigma_from_grip` builds the grip band as `hypot(mu, sigma)` where `mu` is the **absolute session pace level** (~90 s), and the builder evaluates the grip curve at a hardcoded `x=0` (`scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py:417` calls `grip_lookup(year, gp, session_type, 0)`) — a green-track state that is an extrapolation outside the observed data for nearly every session.

Consequence, measured over all 110 stored 2023 sessions (excursion c2x2 of `explore-physics-go-forward`, RESULT at `.agent-work/explore-physics-go-forward/excursions/c2x2-sigma-chain-pilot/`):

- With `offset_sigma` forced to **exactly zero**, **93/93 curve-fitted sessions still produce a band > 10 s** against a 0.1–0.2 s deficit — the ~90 s lap-time floor dominates the band regardless of fit quality.
- This — not the #678/#687 σ blow-up tail — is what makes the #712/#670 grip-term diagnostic vacuous at the **median** (shipped band median 105.6 s).
- Fixing #678 and #687 completely would still leave the diagnostic vacuous; this defect is independent of both and dominates.
- `x=0` is additionally the worst available evaluation point: under any contract it re-manufactures blow-ups through backward extrapolation of the exponential (measured p90 8.3e24 s under a candidate contract at x=0).

## Scope of the fix

Minimal correctness: stop folding the pace *level* into an uncertainty band, and move evaluation off hardcoded `x=0` to an in-data point. **The full replacement consumer contract (e.g. a band keyed to evolution magnitude, measured at median 8.66 s in c2x2) is a separate owner decision and is explicitly NOT settled by this issue** — c2x2 measured one candidate; alternatives exist.

Related: #712 (the vacuity this explains), #687 (gate), #678 (fit identifiability), #663 (the G module).
","number":721,"state":"OPEN","title":"physics: grip band folds absolute pace level into sigma and evaluates at hardcoded x=0 — dominant, previously unfiled cause of #712 vacuity"}
