# Design Spec — Physics measurement-fidelity round: the go-forward build (pre-Build-2)

## Confirmation

- **Status: CONFIRMED**
- Confirmed by: owner (fredcai6), in-session explicit confirmation following the full section-by-section approval pass and the 53-finding triage
- Date: 2026-08-01
- Critic findings dispositioned: YES — 53/53 (50 EDIT applied in this document, 1 REJECT with reason [S8], IF1 partial-reject with reason; 0 RE-EXPLORE)
- Assumptions exercised: per-corner term weekend-stability and estimability (ICC 0.999, split-half r 0.997, independent reproduction); prediction-ladder rung values against held-out truth with oracle + substitution controls; σ-chain levers and their order (lap gate dominant, priors insufficient, consumer-units fix 12×) across 110 sessions and the g4/g5 harnesses; the three defect patterns across five independent pipelines; line-null in quali with shuffled-datum control; ICC frame correction (0.49 → 0.18 driver-only); capability floor (93% of per-corner σ unreachable by the global family, simulator-swept)
- Assumptions accepted untested: prior-year transfer across a regulation change (2021→2022 unrun until W6 stage 2); cross-year census/boundary stability (rides the W1 issue as commander notes, per owner ruling); the frontier itself as a predictable object (A2 spans 4.5× — next round); between-weekend driver-layer error (the weekends-to-reliability projection is an upper bound); defect-taxonomy completeness beyond "no recurrence of the three known patterns"

## Intent

Restore trust in what the physics views measure, then rebuild the driver/car prediction inputs on the de-biased foundation — the pre-Build-2 pre-work the owner called for after #670's near-null, now executed as evidence rather than plan. "Done" feels like: the three repair branches merged and the stores rebuilt on them; a per-corner correction table producing two working products (a post-preceding-race early look and an end-of-Friday look); grip uncertainty made honest and usable — with the 0.1–0.2 s deficit scale as the aspiration, not the acceptance bar: falling short of it after the repairs is a finding about where the remaining inflation lives, not a failure of the round (owner ruling, mirrored in H4's deny-reading); standing instruments that catch the next measurement defect automatically; and the #713 held-out diagnostic re-run on the clean substrate so the Build-2 decision is made with real numbers.

**This spec is deliberately hypothesis-framed (owner directive).** Every work stream names the hypothesis it chases and the reading that confirms or denies it. At execution's end, the register below is re-scored and becomes the entry board for the next exploration round — this round is one turn of an intentionally recursive de-confounding exercise, not a terminal plan.

## Exploration record (digest)

**Standing caveat (owner, at approval):** every null and rejection below is conditioned on the code and model stack as of 2026-08-01 — the right call against today's pipeline, not a permanent verdict. Each de-confounding step re-opens the questions downstream of it; future exploration rounds may and should revisit any entry here whose conditioning has changed. (This is the round's own recursive posture applied to its own conclusions.)

- **Cycles run:** 4 — shotgun (29 ideas, 4 excursions) → refine ×3 (pilot the two load-bearing predictions; chase the relocated problem; quantify the product rungs) + an owner-authorized mid-exploration repair wave (3 commanders). 15 crewed excursions/repairs total, all verified at source.
- **Excursion answers (scoped nulls preserved):**
  - x1/c2x1: same-κ-basis and canonical-κ refits do NOT move the field-shared per-corner σ (4.94→4.95 m/s; CI excludes >6%); NO global lateral curve can reach >7% of it (simulator-swept floor). Canonicalization DOES collapse cross-circuit disagreement 9×. x1's demand-side mechanism was retracted (shared-variable correlation artifact).
  - x2/c2x2/c3x2: grip-σ blow-up = ridge (mostly manufactured by dirty laps) + gate defect + a dominant, previously-unfiled consumer units defect + a record-schema numeric trap. Priors are nearly free but insufficient; the flying-lap gate is the big σ lever (evolution σ 3.37→0.29 s); fuel ruled out; sign defect (D>0) survives everything else.
  - c3x1/c4x2: the 0.88 g residue is 99.4% corner-stable, estimable from one weekend (ICC 0.999); ~⅓–⅖ is stable utilization (pedal channels, friction-circle sign); post-removal residual splits car 14.8% / driver 14.7%, both real, driver layer thin and structurally relative at 2-car teams; #717's ICC 0.49 corrected to 0.18 driver-only (frame-manufactured).
  - c3x3: line choice ≈ zero IN QUALI (apex paths converge to ~noise floor); S30 lives at race sessions; controls prevented a false headline.
  - c4x1: prediction ladder vs held-out truth — geometry 0.38 → prior-year 0.86 → post-race 0.86 (cross-circuit transfer null) → +FP1 0.99 → +FP2 0.996. Shape saturates; amplitude grows (×1.11–1.28). One year-step, same reg era only.
  - c4x3: the defect patterns recur (#685 dirty-lap bias; #557 worst ridge + v=0 anchoring + falsified stationarity docstring; #591 live; #592 clean-billed); ribbon κ-datum carries ±9%/41% unsigned per-corner error (κ-datum elimination still live); "Italy 1.74×" retired as tail artifact; same-station reads NOT sufficient (fast-sweeper curvature over-read).
  - x3/x4 (research): our #719 pitfall is structurally absent from optimal-control lap sims (single jointly-solved κ); S12/S13 instruments have no documented analog (novel, not catch-up); grip's saturation form is standard; the condition data (track temp, wet fraction, overnight gap) was already collected and unwired.
- **Rejected approaches, with reasons:** S1 capability-side refit (superseded — mechanism proven wrong half); canonical-κ as the per-corner fix (measured null; retained as calibration hygiene); unit engineering (basis-invariant wall, from #717); fuel as |D| inflator (races best by 4×); teammate-centering as reference (standing, #717); cross-circuit within-season transfer for the early look (blending it in worsens the prior-year rung).
- **Open threads carried:** 2021→2022 reg-change stress test of the prior-year rung; predicting the frontier itself (A2 spans 4.5×); field-common stable utilization (needs layout-change/wet-dry design); S30 race-session line test; consumer-contract final choice; surface-features backfill; the two c4x3 issue filings.

## Chosen design

- **Per-section approval:** ALL sections APPROVED by owner in the one-by-one pass (2026-08-01), each with its amendments recorded in place: Intent (deficit-scale as aspiration), Exploration record (conditioning caveat), W0 (merge delegation + proactive cleanup + regression-tripwire H0), W1 (interface hybrid @settled/human; any-session producer), W2, W3, W4, W5 (H8 restated at concept level), W6 (Build-2 timing note), register, testing pathways, out-of-scope. Note on W0 authority (re: finding IF17): the owner's merge delegation was given in conversation independently of this spec's confirm gate and the repair branches carried their own per-branch verification — the delegation stands on that evidence, not on this document's confirmation status.

Two gates, three build streams, one issue chain (structure per critic findings S2/S15): **W0 and W6 are GATES** (single verifiable tasks bounding the round), **W1/W2/W3 are the build streams** (the genuinely new design), **W4 is an ordered chain over its existing issues**, and W5's content is split between W1 (census), W6 (evaluation), and the register (the chase). New issues are cut ONLY for: the track book (W1), the dashboard (W3), the simulator ordinal wiring (W1 deliverable), the surface-features backfill, and the two c4x3 filings. Each reused issue gets a comment linking it to its stream and this spec.

**Status at spec time:** the merge half is DONE (2026-08-01, attempt-1 + finisher): three clean merges on main, #723 ridden, #722 rebased to its own branch to land after the stamped rebuild (finding IF10), H0's merge-stage table exact, push in flight. File the two c4x3-recommended issues (station-join/lap-rejection cluster; fast-sweeper curvature over-read). **Proactively fold in related cleanup from the touched issues where it aids the following work (owner steer):** #723's stale-diagnostic-prose fix and #722's `compose_and_persist_weekend` refactor ride this stream (test-led, bounded); issue close-outs remain owner calls.

- **H0 (regression tripwire, not bit-exactness — owner steer):** each branch's pinned behavioral diff should be *recognizable* in the combined rebuild (ribbon coverage 440/440 with `lap_supply` flags; R2's 14/110 rain flips; R3's order-of-magnitude band drop). **Where the fixes jointly touch the same numbers — clean laps feeding grip fits whose bands R3 re-keys — interactions are EXPECTED and bit-level agreement with per-branch pins is NOT assumed.** *Confirm:* divergences from per-branch pins are explained by named interactions with no regression. *Deny reading:* an unexplained divergence or regression → stop and diagnose before any W1/W2 measurement is trusted.

### W1 — The track book (per-corner correction table) + its two products

**Critic-driven amendments (all dispositioned EDIT unless noted):**
- **Corner identity, resolved (IF3/IF16):** the table keys on a **pinned census version** — one frozen census per (circuit, regulation era), stored once and *not* re-derived per weekend; the identity field is `layout_id` (assigned from the hash function — the runtime dataclass has no `layout_content_hash` field). Layout change is detected by an **explicit separate check** against the pinned census (boundary-distance comparison on the new weekend's reference lap), never by hash re-derivation. **Commander notes riding the W1 issue (owner ruling — in-issue, not spec-gating):** measure cross-year boundary/hash stability early (T2 — noting same-track same-year weekends barely exist; year-to-year machinery change is the dominant confound and the 0.86 rung already absorbs it empirically), and calibrate the `CornerAlignmentError` threshold against the c2x1/c3x1 census-match data as the labelled corpus (T13).
- **Funded deliverable — simulator ordinal wiring (IF4):** `_compute_speed_caps` today has NO corner-identity input and the shipped generator records the contrary design decision; the distance→ordinal join (SegmentMap `runtime` lookup onto ribbon stations) is an explicit, sized W1 deliverable, and the previously-claimed "terrain-style join" precedent is struck.
- **The two products are deliverables, not query parameters (IF5):** a producer job (runnable per session boundary) plus one named report artifact per look — `track_book_post_race_look` and `track_book_friday_look` — each with an acceptance check that the artifact exists and its ladder score is computed. Runtime activation of the `physics_feature_injection` path is explicitly deferred as a named follow-on (IF14): this round lands the store + artifacts; the live-predictor wiring is a separate decision.
- **As-of contract made testable (T4/T5/T15):** total order = `(year, round, session_ordinal)` spanning weekend boundaries; every written row carries an **input-manifest field** (which sessions' laps fed it) so write-time leakage is auditable; reads return a **status discriminator** — a missing scale row is `status=no_scale`, never a silent `scale=1.0`.
- **Acceptance instrument productionized (T1):** the c4x1 ladder harness graduates from its proto branch into a committed test/script with the metric pinned (see Testing pathways); it is W1's acceptance test, run at build time and at each season extension.

Build the per-corner correction store: shape estimated from prior-year telemetry on a **frozen canonical census + terrain** (one census carried across seasons — half the prior-year error was per-year self-re-derivation), amplitude rescaled by a 1–2-parameter fit on the current weekend's sessions. **Producer cadence is not fixed (owner steer): the producer may run after ANY session boundary, writing the best estimate available as-of that moment — the table always answers with the most information it has, which is almost always more than nothing** (zero current-weekend sessions → the prior-year shape unscaled; each landed session → a refreshed scale row at that as-of). The two named products — the **post-preceding-race early look** and the **end-of-Friday look** — are simply two points on this continuous as-of axis, not a privileged pair; a read at cutoff X resolves the latest scale row at-or-before X (default 1.0), under the strict as-of contract (a read must never see later sessions). The measured ladder (0.86 / 0.99 / 0.996) tells us what each point is *worth*, not which points are allowed. The ideal-lap generator/simulator consumes the correction the same way at whatever cutoff its caller runs at.
- **Interface: design-it-twice panel COMPLETE** (3 designs at `excursions/dit-trackbook-{a-minimal,b-flex,c-caller}/RESULT.md`). Comparison on depth/locality/seam/testability:
  - **A (minimal)** — three functions, two tidy tables; the whole rung ladder resolves behind ONE cross-boundary read. Its load-bearing discovery, **verified at source**: corner identity should reuse `SegmentMap`'s shipped `layout_content_hash` + corner ordinal (epic #659) — reg-change resets fall out of the hash *by construction* — with one new write-time `CornerAlignmentError` gate covering the unshipped Build-3 continuity guarantee (this is where Monaco-class instability fails loudly). As-of/leakage enforced at WRITE time, mirroring the codebase's one existing, boundary-tested physics→evo crossing (`feature_view/read.py` + its import-boundary test). Evidenced cuts: no σ field (K2's lesson: σ ahead of its consumer contract went vacuous twice; S22 is the named future consumer), no FP2 rung (+0.004 measured), no overlay hook, no multi-year fallback chain.
  - **B (evolution)** — immutable identity registry split from a run-keyed value store; rungs as provenance records; an `overlay_layer` table pinned to a `base_run_id` with a **mandatory shrinkage-factor field** (encodes c4x2's near-miss in schema). Its registry centerpiece is, however, superseded by A's verified discovery — `SegmentMap` already IS that registry.
  - **C (caller-first)** — confirmed both consumers land on already-precedented seams (the terrain-style join inside `_compute_speed_caps`, applied after wear-derate since the term is corner-stable; the `physics_feature_injection` idiom for the runtime) and pushed census matching to write time. Largely convergent with A's landings; its independent matcher is superseded by the SegmentMap reuse.
  - **DECISION (owner-ratified; restated per critic findings S3/S10/S11/IF4/IF16): the interface is A, verbatim** — SegmentMap identity (`layout_id` + corner ordinal — the runtime field name, per IF16), three functions, write-time `CornerAlignmentError` gate, write-time as-of, with the two genuine evidenced cuts (no σ field pre-S22, per K2's lesson; no FP2 rung, per the measured +0.004) — **plus B's `overlay_layer` design recorded as a CANDIDATE design (untaken road, not pre-agreed schema)**: the documented starting point for the fingerprint mount when H8 gains a confirmed consumer, symmetric with how the σ cut names S22. C's runtime-read landing stands as caller confirmation; its simulator-landing precedent claim was corrected by IF4 (the ordinal wiring is new, funded work, not an existing seam).
    @grade: settled/human · leans W1,W5,W6
  - Untaken roads recorded: B's run-id provenance lineage (richer than `model_version`; revisit if re-estimation churn becomes real); a read-side match-quality field; any σ field pre-S22.
- Skipped design-it-twice, with reasons: grip-record re-key (c2x2's four-arm experiment already measured the alternatives; `v1_direct` is the evidenced winner); instruments interface (single consumer today — a boundary with one implementer is a guess; solidify at the second consumer).
- **H1 (year-to-year):** the prior-year shape holds ≈0.86 held-out at unchanged layouts *within a regulation era*; the 2021→2022 crossing degrades gracefully rather than collapsing. *Confirm:* extend the ladder across the reg boundary + ≥6 more circuits. *Deny reading:* reg-era resets become first-class in the table's keying (the flexibility design anticipates this).
- **H2 (amplitude):** a 1–2-parameter FP1 scale captures the FP1→Q amplitude growth (×1.11–1.28 measured) with no per-corner refit. *Confirm:* Friday-look ladder score ≥0.99 reproduced at new circuits via scale-only update. *Deny:* amplitude is corner-structured → per-corner-class scale, revisit.
- **H3 (utilization covariates):** the pedal channels (R² 0.38–0.41 measured, correlational) survive as *predictive* covariates of the table's term out-of-circuit. *Confirm/deny:* held-out circuit prediction with/without pedal features. Denial does not sink W1 (the table works without attribution); it re-scopes the attribution question for the next round.

### W2 — The grip uncertainty chain, in the proven order

**Critic-driven amendments:** (T7/IF15) W2 gains a **separately scored acceptance artifact** — the band-distribution report (median/p90/vacuous count/plausible-|D| count) recomputed at each chain step on the stamped substrate, with the harnesses hard-failing (not skipping) when the store is absent; the deficit scale remains aspiration-not-bar (owner ruling) but harness *validity* failures are stop-the-line. (T19) Per-step deltas are recorded so a later round can tell which link did the work. (T20) The flying-lap gate's parameters are pre-registered and the retained-session fraction is reported beside every band distribution — the "majority of gated sessions" reading may not be manufactured by exclusion. (S12) The |D| prior is restated as a **numerical-stability guard**, not a chain element. (IF6) W2's in-round σ consumer is named: the held-out diagnostic script already folds a grip σ term into its predictive σ — W6 stage 1 consumes W2's honest band through that existing path, and the final consumer contract remains the owner's decision at this stream's close, taken on the measured evidence (c2x2's candidate + this stream's report). (W0 evidence) The lap gate is a pattern-reuse of R1's design onto grip's own SQL lap reader — the code paths are disjoint.

(1) Flying-lap gate on the grip fit's input, reusing R1's gate+fallback design for the quali lap-supply problem (13/14 Q sessions go thin under a naive gate); (2) the D≤0 sign gate (physicality: rubbering-in cannot slow a dry track); (3) V1 reparameterized fit **with the record re-key** (`GripEstimateRecord` moves to in-data coordinates — x=0 keying is numerically non-viable for this curve family, measured); (4) a physical-σ acceptance gate (only now meaningful); (5) a mild |D| prior (~N(0, 2 s), nearly free, measured); (6) wire the condition data: track-temp regressor (#686 thread 2), overnight-gap term, continuous wetness (already exposed by R2).
- Interface note: the re-keyed record is a **schema change with one producer and known consumers** (g4/g5 harnesses, band builder, `get_grip_at` readers) — c2x2's `v1_direct` arm is the adapter shape; consumers enumerated in R3's topology report.
- **H4 (the lap-set hypothesis):** with clean laps + sign gate + V1 + re-key, the grip band lands at deficit scale on the majority of gated sessions without any prior doing heavy lifting (c3x2 measured 31/74 ≤0.2 s on σ with the gate alone). *Confirm:* post-W2 band distribution on the W0 substrate. *Deny:* the residual inflator is real physics (track state) → the condition-wiring step (6) is the next lever, and #686's circuit-conditional scale question re-opens.
- **H5 (condition wiring):** track-temp + overnight-gap + wetness regressors absorb a measurable share of the inter-session offset the current model eats blindly. *Confirm/deny:* held-out log-score of the grip fit with/without, per #663's harnesses.

### W3 — The standing instrument (dashboard, with the tripwire as its top layer)

**Critic-driven amendments:** (S9) the tripwire is folded into the dashboard as its top-layer check plus a committed acceptance assertion — one instrument, one lifecycle. (IF7) "Standing" is now mechanical: a post-store-rebuild hook plus a per-race-weekend scheduled run, both named in the W3 issue. (IF8/T8) Before any null read counts: the dashboard must **re-find the round's own known anomalies** on the stamped substrate (a frozen known-anomaly registry ships with it — the #719 offsets, the #721 band pathology as-was, the c3x2 contamination signature) and recover a **seeded anomaly at stated magnitude**; H6's deny branch is inadmissible until both pass. (T21) The tripwire layer additionally needs a measured real-data false-positive rate on the post-W1 substrate (W1 moves the ideal it checks against) before it is trusted standing. (T1) The dashboard graduates from the proto branch into committed code with the estimator-safety rules as fixtures.

The field-beats-ideal tripwire (sign-based, no calibration needed) and the residual-decomposition dashboard (field-shared / car / driver / noise), built from the consolidated excursion instrument (branch `proto/c4x2-residual-detangle` lineage) with the estimator-safety rules attached: every residual-after-sweep rung carries its shrink factor plus a model-free split-half beside it; every correlation names its frame and substitutes shared variables out.
- Runs read-only over the W0 stores + W1 table; no production-path coupling. Interface deliberately thin until a second consumer exists (stated above).
- **H6 (instrument value):** the dashboard, run over the rebuilt stores, surfaces at least one previously-unknown field-shared anomaly (the round found one per cycle while hand-cranked). *Confirm:* first standing run's findings list. *Deny reading:* fidelity really is restored at current sensitivity — which is itself the Build-2 green light this spec exists to earn.

### W4 — The same three cures for the other views (an ordered issue chain, not a stream — per S2)

**Restated:** W4 is executed as its four existing issues (#685, #557, #591, #592-closeout) in that order, each with the cure named below as a comment linking to this spec; no new issues, no shared interface. **Exception to "rides behind" (IF11): #557's `a_t` re-key is a W6 PRECONDITION** — W6 evaluates the driver term against the car side of the join, and a knowingly-mis-signed car axis would make H10's null uninterpretable. (T12) H7 is softened to the testable claim — **no recurrence of the three known patterns** in a post-fix re-audit — with a defect-class-agnostic goodness-of-fit screen recorded as a next-round instrument candidate (a completeness claim needs an instrument not derived from the known failure set).

#685: gate the reference-lap pool to flying laps (reuse R1's design; matched-count control proved lap SET not COUNT) + the separate persistence-floor residue. #557: re-key the traction descriptor off v=0 to an in-data reference speed (~30 m/s; the grip anchoring cure, no refit) and correct the falsified "track-stable" docstring/consumers (`a_t` is circuit-dominated 22:1 — `build_car_basis`/#512-vector consumers must stop reading it as a car axis); the corner-indexed refit remains #557's own follow-on. #591: replace the flat σ-floor with the audit's local-scatter statistic (external-anchor-compatible, already measured at 7× within-session range). #592: close as clean-billed for Layer-1; file the LateralView per-sample-σ residue separately.
- **H7 (pattern generality):** the three cures transfer with no new defect classes appearing — i.e. the round's taxonomy (basis, conditioning, lap hygiene) is complete for the frontier views. *Confirm:* post-fix re-audit table clean. *Deny:* a fourth pattern → next round's cluster A.

### W5 — The driver axis: level EVALUATED (shipping gated on W6), fingerprint as a live hypothesis stream

**Amended per S5/IF13/T14 (three lenses converged; accepted):** the driver **level** term is NOT shipped ahead of the gate. It is built as an **evaluated arm inside W6** — seam: the `physics_feature_injection` field idiom; shrinkage: 0.5 per c4x2's measurement (raw hurts); acceptance: held-out improvement in W6's ablation design; rollback: the arm simply doesn't ship on deny. It ships on W6-confirm as the confirm *action*. (The +0.69-vs-+0.67 warrant is restated with its context in the Numbers appendix — it is a cross-circuit transfer correlation against its own split-half ceiling, not a 0.02 margin claim.) (IF9) One **cheap alternative-representation probe is funded here**: the corner-class coarse-grain fingerprint over existing data, so H8 has at least one runnable confirm/deny action this round. (S6) The backfill and multi-season instrument extension now serve W6 stage 2 directly — nothing in this stream is build-ahead without an in-round consumer. The corner-resolved **fingerprint stays an active chase, not a parked idea (owner ruling)**: the residual layers plausibly encode driver approach and car dynamics weekend-to-weekend. Its prerequisites are built here: the frozen census (W1), surface-features backfill beyond 2022–2023, and the multi-season extension of the instrument (seat-changers give the only non-relative cross-team scale at 2-car teams — structural, measured).
- **H8 (owner's hypothesis, primary for the next round — stated at CONCEPT level, owner clarification 2026-08-01):** *there exists transferable knowledge between corners on different tracks* — some representation in which driver-approach and/or car-dynamics structure carries across circuits and weekends. **The hypothesis is about the concept, NOT today's fingerprint implementation** — the current corner-grain machinery is one candidate representation among several and is freely revisable like every other model in this project. Current evidence reads against transfer *in the representations tried so far* (corner-shape doesn't transfer cross-circuit, c4x2; per-physical-corner skill didn't generalize to families, #717-era) — all representation-conditioned nulls, none touching the concept. Candidate representations for the chase: multi-season corner-grain (needs the prerequisites built here), coarser grains (corner-class, phase-of-corner), pedal-signature spaces (the channels H3 opens), the energy-archetype vocabulary (#682), race-session line signatures (H9). *Confirm:* ANY representation showing held-out cross-track transfer of a driver/car layer above its noise floor. *Deny reading:* only the representations actually exercised, enumerated at re-scoring — the concept dies solely by exhaustion, not by any single null.
- **H9 (race-session line):** driver line variation is measurable in races (quali suppressed it to ~noise). *Confirm/deny:* c3x3's instrument on race sessions, unchanged.

### W6 (gate) — The exit gate, two-stage

**Amended per IF2/T3/T14/T16/IF12/IF1:**
- **Stage 1 (single-season, on the stamped substrate):** the held-out driver-term diagnostic re-run on 2022–2023 (the surface-features coverage that exists), with a full **ablation design** (T14): no-driver baseline, leave-one-component-out arms (−W1 table, −W2 σ, −level term), and a **sensitivity-perturbation arm bounding the W1 term's uncarried σ** (T16: re-run at plausible scale perturbations). Preconditions: W0's stamped rebuild AND #557's `a_t` re-key (IF11).
- **Stage 2 (the true #713 multi-season slice):** gated on the **surface-features backfill (2018–2021, 2024–2026)**, which this gate now sequences as its own funded precondition (T3) — this is what makes W6's product the experiment #713 actually specifies (IF2), and what makes H1 scoreable (T10, via 2021 coverage).
- **Closing deliverable (IF12/IF1):** the **re-scored hypothesis register** (`REGISTER_RESCORE.md`), produced by the executing lead and disposed by the owner — the Build-2 decision is made BY THE OWNER at that artifact, on that evidence; there is deliberately no automatic accepting state (owner posture: Build-2 may be a couple of rounds out, and that's fine — the gate's job is to make the decision evidenced, not to make it).
- **H10 (the round's thesis):** de-biasing the reference and honest σ turn

- **Interface: design-it-twice panel COMPLETE** (3 designs at `excursions/dit-trackbook-{a-minimal,b-flex,c-caller}/RESULT.md`). Comparison on depth/locality/seam/testability:
  - **A (minimal)** — three functions, two tidy tables; the whole rung ladder resolves behind ONE cross-boundary read. Its load-bearing discovery, **verified at source**: corner identity should reuse `SegmentMap`'s shipped `layout_content_hash` + corner ordinal (epic #659) — reg-change resets fall out of the hash *by construction* — with one new write-time `CornerAlignmentError` gate covering the unshipped Build-3 continuity guarantee (this is where Monaco-class instability fails loudly). As-of/leakage enforced at WRITE time, mirroring the codebase's one existing, boundary-tested physics→evo crossing (`feature_view/read.py` + its import-boundary test). Evidenced cuts: no σ field (K2's lesson: σ ahead of its consumer contract went vacuous twice; S22 is the named future consumer), no FP2 rung (+0.004 measured), no overlay hook, no multi-year fallback chain.
  - **B (evolution)** — immutable identity registry split from a run-keyed value store; rungs as provenance records; an `overlay_layer` table pinned to a `base_run_id` with a **mandatory shrinkage-factor field** (encodes c4x2's near-miss in schema). Its registry centerpiece is, however, superseded by A's verified discovery — `SegmentMap` already IS that registry.
  - **C (caller-first)** — confirmed both consumers land on already-precedented seams (the terrain-style join inside `_compute_speed_caps`, applied after wear-derate since the term is corner-stable; the `physics_feature_injection` idiom for the runtime) and pushed census matching to write time. Largely convergent with A's landings; its independent matcher is superseded by the SegmentMap reuse.
  - **DECISION (owner-ratified; restated per critic findings S3/S10/S11/IF4/IF16): the interface is A, verbatim** — SegmentMap identity (`layout_id` + corner ordinal — the runtime field name, per IF16), three functions, write-time `CornerAlignmentError` gate, write-time as-of, with the two genuine evidenced cuts (no σ field pre-S22, per K2's lesson; no FP2 rung, per the measured +0.004) — **plus B's `overlay_layer` design recorded as a CANDIDATE design (untaken road, not pre-agreed schema)**: the documented starting point for the fingerprint mount when H8 gains a confirmed consumer, symmetric with how the σ cut names S22. C's runtime-read landing stands as caller confirmation; its simulator-landing precedent claim was corrected by IF4 (the ordinal wiring is new, funded work, not an existing seam).
    @grade: settled/human · leans W1,W5,W6
  - Untaken roads recorded: B's run-id provenance lineage (richer than `model_version`; revisit if re-estimation churn becomes real); a read-side match-quality field; any σ field pre-S22.
- Skipped design-it-twice, with reasons: grip-record re-key (c2x2's four-arm experiment already measured the alternatives; `v1_direct` is the evidenced winner); instruments interface (single consumer today — a boundary with one implementer is a guess; solidify at the second consumer).
- **H1 (year-to-year):** the prior-year shape holds ≈0.86 held-out at unchanged layouts *within a regulation era*; the 2021→2022 crossing degrades gracefully rather than collapsing. *Confirm:* extend the ladder across the reg boundary + ≥6 more circuits. *Deny reading:* reg-era resets become first-class in the table's keying (the flexibility design anticipates this).
- **H2 (amplitude):** a 1–2-parameter FP1 scale captures the FP1→Q amplitude growth (×1.11–1.28 measured) with no per-corner refit. *Confirm:* Friday-look ladder score ≥0.99 reproduced at new circuits via scale-only update. *Deny:* amplitude is corner-structured → per-corner-class scale, revisit.
- **H3 (utilization covariates):** the pedal channels (R² 0.38–0.41 measured, correlational) survive as *predictive* covariates of the table's term out-of-circuit. *Confirm/deny:* held-out circuit prediction with/without pedal features. Denial does not sink W1 (the table works without attribution); it re-scopes the attribution question for the next round.

### W2 — The grip uncertainty chain, in the proven order

**Critic-driven amendments:** (T7/IF15) W2 gains a **separately scored acceptance artifact** — the band-distribution report (median/p90/vacuous count/plausible-|D| count) recomputed at each chain step on the stamped substrate, with the harnesses hard-failing (not skipping) when the store is absent; the deficit scale remains aspiration-not-bar (owner ruling) but harness *validity* failures are stop-the-line. (T19) Per-step deltas are recorded so a later round can tell which link did the work. (T20) The flying-lap gate's parameters are pre-registered and the retained-session fraction is reported beside every band distribution — the "majority of gated sessions" reading may not be manufactured by exclusion. (S12) The |D| prior is restated as a **numerical-stability guard**, not a chain element. (IF6) W2's in-round σ consumer is named: the held-out diagnostic script already folds a grip σ term into its predictive σ — W6 stage 1 consumes W2's honest band through that existing path, and the final consumer contract remains the owner's decision at this stream's close, taken on the measured evidence (c2x2's candidate + this stream's report). (W0 evidence) The lap gate is a pattern-reuse of R1's design onto grip's own SQL lap reader — the code paths are disjoint.

(1) Flying-lap gate on the grip fit's input, reusing R1's gate+fallback design for the quali lap-supply problem (13/14 Q sessions go thin under a naive gate); (2) the D≤0 sign gate (physicality: rubbering-in cannot slow a dry track); (3) V1 reparameterized fit **with the record re-key** (`GripEstimateRecord` moves to in-data coordinates — x=0 keying is numerically non-viable for this curve family, measured); (4) a physical-σ acceptance gate (only now meaningful); (5) a mild |D| prior (~N(0, 2 s), nearly free, measured); (6) wire the condition data: track-temp regressor (#686 thread 2), overnight-gap term, continuous wetness (already exposed by R2).
- Interface note: the re-keyed record is a **schema change with one producer and known consumers** (g4/g5 harnesses, band builder, `get_grip_at` readers) — c2x2's `v1_direct` arm is the adapter shape; consumers enumerated in R3's topology report.
- **H4 (the lap-set hypothesis):** with clean laps + sign gate + V1 + re-key, the grip band lands at deficit scale on the majority of gated sessions without any prior doing heavy lifting (c3x2 measured 31/74 ≤0.2 s on σ with the gate alone). *Confirm:* post-W2 band distribution on the W0 substrate. *Deny:* the residual inflator is real physics (track state) → the condition-wiring step (6) is the next lever, and #686's circuit-conditional scale question re-opens.
- **H5 (condition wiring):** track-temp + overnight-gap + wetness regressors absorb a measurable share of the inter-session offset the current model eats blindly. *Confirm/deny:* held-out log-score of the grip fit with/without, per #663's harnesses.

### W3 — The standing instrument (dashboard, with the tripwire as its top layer)

**Critic-driven amendments:** (S9) the tripwire is folded into the dashboard as its top-layer check plus a committed acceptance assertion — one instrument, one lifecycle. (IF7) "Standing" is now mechanical: a post-store-rebuild hook plus a per-race-weekend scheduled run, both named in the W3 issue. (IF8/T8) Before any null read counts: the dashboard must **re-find the round's own known anomalies** on the stamped substrate (a frozen known-anomaly registry ships with it — the #719 offsets, the #721 band pathology as-was, the c3x2 contamination signature) and recover a **seeded anomaly at stated magnitude**; H6's deny branch is inadmissible until both pass. (T21) The tripwire layer additionally needs a measured real-data false-positive rate on the post-W1 substrate (W1 moves the ideal it checks against) before it is trusted standing. (T1) The dashboard graduates from the proto branch into committed code with the estimator-safety rules as fixtures.

The field-beats-ideal tripwire (sign-based, no calibration needed) and the residual-decomposition dashboard (field-shared / car / driver / noise), built from the consolidated excursion instrument (branch `proto/c4x2-residual-detangle` lineage) with the estimator-safety rules attached: every residual-after-sweep rung carries its shrink factor plus a model-free split-half beside it; every correlation names its frame and substitutes shared variables out.
- Runs read-only over the W0 stores + W1 table; no production-path coupling. Interface deliberately thin until a second consumer exists (stated above).
- **H6 (instrument value):** the dashboard, run over the rebuilt stores, surfaces at least one previously-unknown field-shared anomaly (the round found one per cycle while hand-cranked). *Confirm:* first standing run's findings list. *Deny reading:* fidelity really is restored at current sensitivity — which is itself the Build-2 green light this spec exists to earn.

### W4 — The same three cures for the other views (an ordered issue chain, not a stream — per S2)

**Restated:** W4 is executed as its four existing issues (#685, #557, #591, #592-closeout) in that order, each with the cure named below as a comment linking to this spec; no new issues, no shared interface. **Exception to "rides behind" (IF11): #557's `a_t` re-key is a W6 PRECONDITION** — W6 evaluates the driver term against the car side of the join, and a knowingly-mis-signed car axis would make H10's null uninterpretable. (T12) H7 is softened to the testable claim — **no recurrence of the three known patterns** in a post-fix re-audit — with a defect-class-agnostic goodness-of-fit screen recorded as a next-round instrument candidate (a completeness claim needs an instrument not derived from the known failure set).

#685: gate the reference-lap pool to flying laps (reuse R1's design; matched-count control proved lap SET not COUNT) + the separate persistence-floor residue. #557: re-key the traction descriptor off v=0 to an in-data reference speed (~30 m/s; the grip anchoring cure, no refit) and correct the falsified "track-stable" docstring/consumers (`a_t` is circuit-dominated 22:1 — `build_car_basis`/#512-vector consumers must stop reading it as a car axis); the corner-indexed refit remains #557's own follow-on. #591: replace the flat σ-floor with the audit's local-scatter statistic (external-anchor-compatible, already measured at 7× within-session range). #592: close as clean-billed for Layer-1; file the LateralView per-sample-σ residue separately.
- **H7 (pattern generality):** the three cures transfer with no new defect classes appearing — i.e. the round's taxonomy (basis, conditioning, lap hygiene) is complete for the frontier views. *Confirm:* post-fix re-audit table clean. *Deny:* a fourth pattern → next round's cluster A.

### W5 — The driver axis: level EVALUATED (shipping gated on W6), fingerprint as a live hypothesis stream

**Amended per S5/IF13/T14 (three lenses converged; accepted):** the driver **level** term is NOT shipped ahead of the gate. It is built as an **evaluated arm inside W6** — seam: the `physics_feature_injection` field idiom; shrinkage: 0.5 per c4x2's measurement (raw hurts); acceptance: held-out improvement in W6's ablation design; rollback: the arm simply doesn't ship on deny. It ships on W6-confirm as the confirm *action*. (The +0.69-vs-+0.67 warrant is restated with its context in the Numbers appendix — it is a cross-circuit transfer correlation against its own split-half ceiling, not a 0.02 margin claim.) (IF9) One **cheap alternative-representation probe is funded here**: the corner-class coarse-grain fingerprint over existing data, so H8 has at least one runnable confirm/deny action this round. (S6) The backfill and multi-season instrument extension now serve W6 stage 2 directly — nothing in this stream is build-ahead without an in-round consumer. The corner-resolved **fingerprint stays an active chase, not a parked idea (owner ruling)**: the residual layers plausibly encode driver approach and car dynamics weekend-to-weekend. Its prerequisites are built here: the frozen census (W1), surface-features backfill beyond 2022–2023, and the multi-season extension of the instrument (seat-changers give the only non-relative cross-team scale at 2-car teams — structural, measured).
- **H8 (owner's hypothesis, primary for the next round — stated at CONCEPT level, owner clarification 2026-08-01):** *there exists transferable knowledge between corners on different tracks* — some representation in which driver-approach and/or car-dynamics structure carries across circuits and weekends. **The hypothesis is about the concept, NOT today's fingerprint implementation** — the current corner-grain machinery is one candidate representation among several and is freely revisable like every other model in this project. Current evidence reads against transfer *in the representations tried so far* (corner-shape doesn't transfer cross-circuit, c4x2; per-physical-corner skill didn't generalize to families, #717-era) — all representation-conditioned nulls, none touching the concept. Candidate representations for the chase: multi-season corner-grain (needs the prerequisites built here), coarser grains (corner-class, phase-of-corner), pedal-signature spaces (the channels H3 opens), the energy-archetype vocabulary (#682), race-session line signatures (H9). *Confirm:* ANY representation showing held-out cross-track transfer of a driver/car layer above its noise floor. *Deny reading:* only the representations actually exercised, enumerated at re-scoring — the concept dies solely by exhaustion, not by any single null.
- **H9 (race-session line):** driver line variation is measurable in races (quali suppressed it to ~noise). *Confirm/deny:* c3x3's instrument on race sessions, unchanged.

(IF8/T8) Before any null read counts: the dashboard must **re-find the round's own known anomalies** on the stamped substrate (a frozen known-anomaly registry ships with it — the #719 offsets, the #721 band pathology as-was, the c3x2 contamination signature) and recover a **seeded anomaly at stated magnitude**; H6's deny branch is inadmissible until both pass. (T1) The dashboard graduates from the proto branch into committed code with the estimator-safety rules as fixtures.

The field-beats-ideal tripwire (sign-based, no calibration needed) and the residual-decomposition dashboard (field-shared / car / driver / noise), built from the consolidated excursion instrument (branch `proto/c4x2-residual-detangle` lineage) with the estimator-safety rules attached: every residual-after-sweep rung carries its shrink factor plus a model-free split-half beside it; every correlation names its frame and substitutes shared variables out.

# RESULT — r3-721-consumer-units (repair commander, issue #721)

**Verdict: FIXED.** Both defects named in #721 are corrected as a minimal
correctness fix, no new consumer contract introduced. Test-led, independently
implemented and independently reviewed (both APPROVE), independently
re-verified by the commander at every integration point, and measured
before/after on real archived production data (not just synthetic fixtures).

**Branch:** `fix/721-grip-band-units`, worktree
`C:/Programs/f1Brainz/.claude/worktrees/fix-721-grip-band-units`, based on
local `main` tip at branch creation (`3541d292`). **NOT pushed, no PR** —
committed locally per the launch order. Two commits:

- `a5b24249b2d2765d65b87e7919d79e05c679c22d` — the fix itself (6 files).
- `9fae4c9d` — a one-line architecture-map reconcile-log entry (verified no-op).

---

## What changed

### 1. Units defect fixed
`onesided_sigma_from_grip` (`src/physics/utilization/class_utilization_observable.py`)
computed `hypot(mu, sigma)`, where `mu` — verified by reading `get_grip_at`'s
body directly, not assumed — is `get_grip_at`'s **fitted absolute session pace
level** (`session_offset + curve_asymptote*(1-exp(-curve_rate*x))`,
`session_offset` on the order of ~90s), not a grip delta. Folding a ~90s
absolute level into what should be a small uncertainty scale was the units
bug. **Fix:** the function now takes `sigma` only and returns `abs(sigma)`;
`mu` is still read by both production callers but never enters the band's
scale anywhere. Both call sites (`grip_scale_from_store`,
`compute_class_utilization_observable`) and the module's own "Binding
pre-ruling" docstring section (which previously asserted the `hypot` formula
as deliberate design) were corrected to match.

### 2. Evaluation-point defect fixed
The one production caller
(`scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py`'s
`compose_and_persist_weekend`) evaluated the grip curve at hardcoded `x=0` —
a backward-extrapolation trap outside the field-pooled fit's observed support
(`grip_baseline.py` documents `x->0` as the extrapolated "green-track" limit,
never an observed lap). **Fix:** `make_grip_lookup`'s `_lookup` closure now
accepts `laps: Optional[int]`; the production call site now passes `None`
instead of the literal `0`. When `laps is None`, the closure reads the
session's own already-stored `cumulative_track_laps_max` (via a new
`grip_store.session_cumulative_track_laps_max()` helper — no schema change,
just a new read of an existing column) and evaluates at
`round(GRIP_EVAL_LAPS_FRACTION * max_laps)`. Falls back to `None`
(soft-degrade, unchanged philosophy) if the max is unavailable.

**`get_grip_at` itself is completely unchanged** (confirmed zero-diff by both
crew members and the commander) — its general
`(year, gp_name, session_type, cumulative_track_laps)` contract for
explicit-x callers (e.g. `test_grip_heldout.py`'s nearest-neighbor
comparisons) is untouched.

---

## Evaluation-point decision: `GRIP_EVAL_LAPS_FRACTION = 0.5`

**Surfaced prominently, as requested.** Production's `GripEstimateRecord`
schema stores only `cumulative_track_laps_max` per session — no min, no
percentiles of the underlying per-lap x distribution (those exist only in
c2x2's throwaway excursion measurement, never in any production store). The
only in-data point computable from the already-stored schema without new
plumbing is a fraction of `cumulative_track_laps_max`.

**Chosen: `round(0.5 * cumulative_track_laps_max)`** — a median-of-observed-
range proxy (rubber-laying is roughly monotonic in cumulative_track_laps
across a session, so the midpoint of `[~0, max]` approximates the median of
observed x values). This is the fraction the team-lead brief itself
recommended, applied here, not re-derived independently.

**Alternatives considered and rejected** (named as a code comment next to
the constant, not just in this report):
- 0.25 / 0.75 / 1.0 fractions of `cumulative_track_laps_max` — all measured
  within c2x2's own 1.7x spread of each other; the choice among them is not
  load-bearing.
- `x_min` — excluded as unsafe-adjacent to the same backward-extrapolation
  edge this fix removes (even though the specific "collapses to a
  fake-near-zero band by construction" trap c2x2 named is specific to the
  Δ-from-x_min evolution-magnitude CANDIDATE contract, which this fix does
  NOT implement — see Scope below).
- Building real per-lap percentile machinery — out of scope; the store
  schema doesn't carry that data, and adding it would be new plumbing beyond
  a minimal correctness fix.

This decision is recorded inline as `decision:grip-band-eval-point-fraction`
`@grade: guess` (explicitly low-fixedness — revisit freely if per-lap
percentile data ever enters storage).

---

## Hard scope boundary — honored

**No new consumer contract was introduced.** Grepped the full diff and
found no Δ-from-x_min / evolution-magnitude formula anywhere. The existing
contract (a one-sided σ⁺ scale wrapping the unchanged point deficit) is
unchanged in shape — only its two named defective inputs (the units and the
evaluation point) are corrected. The full consumer-contract redesign remains
excursion c3x2's separate, concurrent, unresolved job.

---

## Consumer topology of `g_sigma_onesided` (grepped, verified, not assumed)

| Consumer | Change needed? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py:417` (the only producer call) | **Fixed here** | The defect's origin. |
| `src/physics/utilization/reference_utilization_store.py` | None | Pure store round-trip — persists the column, computes nothing. Tolerates any magnitude. |
| `src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py:_compose_sigma` | None | `sigma_cell = sqrt(sigma0² + shared_floor² + g_sigma_onesided² + sigma_lapsampling²)` — a continuous quadrature sum, no threshold logic. Tolerates the shrink and is the direct beneficiary (#670 already named this exact term as the dominant sigma-inflation source behind #712's vacuity). |
| `scripts/run_heldout_diagnostic_670.py` (lines ~635-641) | **Flagged, not edited** (out of #721's scope) | A hardcoded prose string in the diagnostic's JSON output describes the OLD pathology ("p90 ~ 8e9 and max ~9.6e9") as a fixed narrative. Now factually stale. Filed as **[#723](https://github.com/fredcai6/f1Brainz/issues/723)**. |

---

## Before/after band measurement — real archived production data

Measured directly (not re-derived from the throwaway c2x2 worktree, per the
brief's instruction) against
`.agent-work/archive/2026-07-27-670-season-run/artifacts/scratch/grip_estimates.db`
— the actual output of the real #670 season run. Scope of this archive: **21
sessions, all 2023 Q sessions** (13 curve-fitted "ok" + 8 "thin_fallback";
this archive does not cover other session types or other seasons — a smaller
slice than c2x2's 110-session excursion measurement, but real production
output, not a re-derivation).

| | median | p90 | max | vacuous (>10s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **BEFORE** (shipped, `hypot(mu,sigma)@x=0`) | 109.13s | 3.44e9 | 9.62e9 | **21/21** |
| **AFTER** (fixed, `sigma-only@0.5*max`) | **19.13s** | 5.80e5 | 9.32e8 | **11/21** |

**The median improves substantially (5.7x) and vacuity roughly halves — but
this is NOT a uniform win, and that matters.** Split by fit type:

- **`thin_fallback` (8 sessions, eval-point-invariant — a clean test of the
  units fix alone):** unambiguous win. OLD 77–117s → NEW exactly the stored
  `session_offset_sigma` (6.0s or 24.0s depending on thin/rain inflation).
  5 of 8 now non-vacuous.
- **`ok` / curve-fitted (13 sessions):** median improves (121.7s → 40.2s) but
  **several individual sessions get WORSE, not better**, off `x=0`
  (e.g. Hungary 101.7s → 511,765s; Qatar 114.1s → 684,948s).

**Why, diagnosed not just observed:** `get_grip_at`'s delta-method variance
formula includes a rate-parameter term
`(x * curve_asymptote * exp(-curve_rate*x))² * curve_rate_sigma²`. At
**`x=0` this term is IDENTICALLY ZERO** regardless of how poorly-identified
`curve_rate` is (multiplied by `x=0`). Moving evaluation off `x=0` — exactly
what #721 asks for — legitimately **re-exposes real, pre-existing
rate-parameter ill-conditioning** in a subset of real fits. This is not a
defect in this fix; it is the fix correctly reporting genuine propagated
uncertainty instead of a value `x=0` was structurally (and silently) masking.
It is consistent with, and independently corroborates from a completely
different mechanism, c2x2's own documented finding that the underlying V0
curve fit's point estimate is degenerate for many real 2023 sessions. Fixing
the fit itself is out of #721's scope (named as #678/#687/c3x2 territory).

**Net honest read:** #721's fix does exactly what it was asked to do — the
~90s pace-level floor is gone, the median moves 5.7x, and the worst backward-
extrapolation trap is closed. It does not, and was never scoped to, fix the
separate pre-existing fit-degeneracy problem that a subset of real sessions
still carry.

---

53/53 targeted tests pass, run independently three times (implementer,
reviewer, commander), most recently just before writing this report:

```

tests\unit\physics\test_class_utilization_observable.py ................ [ 30%]
.                                                                        [ 32%]
tests\unit\physics\test_build_class_utilization_observables.py ......... [ 49%]
.                                                                        [ 50%]
tests\unit\physics\layer2\test_grip_store.py ............                [ 73%]
```

The two "negative-evidence" files (`test_grip_batch.py` 13 passed,
`test_grip_heldout.py` 1 passed) are load-bearing: they exercise
`get_grip_at`'s general caller-chosen-x contract and needed **zero edits**,

`hypot(mu,sigma)` behavior were rewritten to pin the new contract; new tests
cover pace-level non-inflation (a dominant `session_offset` never inflates
the band), the `laps=None` eval-point resolution (asserts the closure
resolves to `round(0.5*max)`, not `x=0`), and a before/after characterization
fixture with real numbers in its assertions:
`OLD = math.hypot(*get_grip_at(store,...,0)) = 90.00004499998875`,
`NEW = grip_scale_from_store(store,...,10) = 0.09325207321864559`
(independently re-derived from scratch by the reviewer, matched to full
precision).

**`simplification_limits`:** 2 of the 3 touched files are clean.
`scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py`'s `compose_and_persist_weekend`
fails the strict check (`cyclomatic_complexity=22`, `function_lines=145`) —
confirmed **pre-existing and byte-identical before/after this diff** via two
independent A/B checks (implementer's `git stash`/`pop`; reviewer's
`git show <parent>:<path>` swap). #721's only touch inside that function was
one call-site line (`0` → `None`). Filed separately as

— the actual output of the real #670 season run. Scope of this archive: **21
sessions, all 2023 Q sessions** (13 curve-fitted "ok" + 8 "thin_fallback";
this archive does not cover other session types or other seasons — a smaller
slice than c2x2's 110-session excursion measurement, but real production
output, not a re-derivation).

| | median | p90 | max | vacuous (>10s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **BEFORE** (shipped, `hypot(mu,sigma)@x=0`) | 109.13s | 3.44e9 | 9.62e9 | **21/21** |

formula includes a rate-parameter term

what #721 asks for — legitimately **re-exposes real, pre-existing
rate-parameter ill-conditioning** in a subset of real fits. This is not a
defect in this fix; it is the fix correctly reporting genuine propagated
uncertainty instead of a value `x=0` was structurally (and silently) masking.
It is consistent with, and independently corroborates from a completely
different mechanism, c2x2's own documented finding that the underlying V0
curve fit's point estimate is degenerate for many real 2023 sessions. Fixing
the fit itself is out of #721's scope (named as #678/#687/c3x2 territory).

**Net honest read:** #721's fix does exactly what it was asked to do — the
~90s pace-level floor is gone, the median moves 5.7x, and the worst backward-
extrapolation trap is closed. It does not, and was never scoped to, fix the
separate pre-existing fit-degeneracy problem that a subset of real sessions
still carry.

    3. **per-CLASS ABSOLUTE deficits** — a speed deficit (m/s) AND a transit-time deficit (s) —
       given ``v_ideal`` and ``v_real`` on a shared grid.

Units: distances in metres (m), speeds in metres/second (m/s), times in seconds (s).

There is NO DB / session / FastF1 / store I/O here — the SegmentMap is CONSUMED read-only.

Class vocabulary (the ``(2+k)`` classes), in W-column order
-----------------------------------------------------------
    ``("straight", "braking_zone") + segment_map.class_ids``

i.e. the two HARD ``seg_type`` classes followed by the ``k`` corner-severity classes named
verbatim by the map's own ``class_ids`` (never re-invented labels).

Attribution — the single ``(n, 2+k)`` weight matrix ``W``
---------------------------------------------------------

reduction is ``Wᵀ · (per-segment quantity)`` — never an ``argmax`` "dominant class" collapse

gating jackknife measure quantization noise instead of real attribution stability). A hard
``argmax`` view, when wanted, is a DERIVED diagnostic OVER ``W`` (:func:`dominant_class_of`),
never the mechanism.

Each ``W`` row sums to 1.0 by construction — STRAIGHT / BRAKING_ZONE rows are one-hot; CORNER

"time-shares sum to the lap" structural rather than incidental.

Anti-circularity (#628) — the load-bearing contract
----------------------------------------------------
Every deficit is ABSOLUTE: ``mean(v_ideal - v_real)`` for speed and ``Δt_real - Δt_ideal`` for

the real lap is SLOWER than ideal (``v_ideal - v_real > 0``; ``Δt_real - Δt_ideal > 0``).

This core computes NO distributional form (no Gaussian/normality assumption — that is a later
gate); it is pure geometry plus the map's own membership.

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ClassTimeLedger:
    """Class-grain transit-time ledger for one lap over a SegmentMap.

    Attributes
    ----------
    class_ids:
        The ``(2+k)`` class vocabulary in ``W``-column order:
        ``("straight", "braking_zone") + segment_map.class_ids``.
    dt_segment:
        Per-segment transit time (s), shape ``(n_segments,)``. Sums to :attr:`lap_time_s`.
    lap_time_s:
        Whole-lap transit time (s) — the ds/v_avg integral over the profile.
    time_by_class_s:
        ``Wᵀ · dt_segment`` (s), shape ``(2+k,)``. Sums to :attr:`lap_time_s`.
    time_share_by_class:
        ``time_by_class_s / lap_time_s`` (dimensionless), shape ``(2+k,)``. Sums to 1.0 by
        construction (each ``W`` row sums to 1).
    W:
        The ``(n_segments, 2+k)`` attribution matrix used for the reduction.

    n_points_by_class = W.T @ n_pts_seg

    dt_real_seg = _segment_transit_times(segment_map, distance_m, v_real, min_speed_ms)
    time_deficit_seg = dt_real_seg - dt_ideal_seg
    time_deficit_by_class = W.T @ time_deficit_seg

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _CellAggregate:
    """One (driver, class) cell's recency-weighted inputs to the two-way fit.

    ``value`` and ``n_eff`` are exactly the handoff's "recency-weighted cell value" and
    "recency-effective support" (recency-weighted sum of ``n_points``). ``g_sigma_onesided``
    and ``sigma_lapsampling`` are carried through as their own recency-weighted aggregates so
    the sigma composition (invariants 3-4) has a real per-cell number to add, not a
    module-level constant.
    """
    value_column: str,
    *,
    as_of_round: int,
    halflife_rounds: float,
) -> dict[tuple[str, str], _CellAggregate]:
    """Group rows by (driver, class); recency-weight each row, then combine.

    The per-row weight is ``recency * n_points`` -- the same weight defines both the cell
    VALUE's weighted mean and (summed alone, without the value) the cell's recency-effective
    support ``n_eff`` (handoff: "a recency-weighted cell value + a recency-effective support
    n_eff (recency-weighted sum of n_points)"). Rows with a NULL channel value, a NULL
    ``n_points``, or a recorded ``error`` are skipped (not usable observations).
    ``g_sigma_onesided``/``sigma_lapsampling`` are aggregated the same way over rows where
    they are non-NULL; a cell with no non-NULL rows for one of these dormant columns
    aggregates to exactly ``0.0`` (present-but-zero, never dropped -- invariant 4).
    """
    buckets: dict[tuple[str, str], list[tuple[float, float, float, Optional[float], Optional[float]]]] = {}
    for row in rows:
        item = _row_to_bucket_item(row, value_column, as_of_round=as_of_round, halflife_rounds=halflife_rounds)
        if item is None:

        key = (row["driver"], row["class"])
        buckets.setdefault(key, []).append(item)

    out: dict[tuple[str, str], _CellAggregate] = {}
    for key, items in buckets.items():
        aggregate = _combine_bucket(items)
        if aggregate is not None:

    return out

### Grip-G baseline (#663, epic #659 — pipeline stage D) — REGENERATED

Module-leaf under `struct:physics.layer2`: `grip_baseline.py` (grip-baseline
fit), `grip_store.py` (`GripStore`, session-level primary key — see
`decision:grip_estimate_record_session_level_pk`), `grip_batch.py`
(`run_grip_batch`, held-out over `grip_bin_obs` rows in `damage_integrals.db`).
This is **stage D** of the epic-#659 C→D→E→G→H→PANEL quali feature pipeline: the
pooled grip-baseline curves are consumed AS-IS by **stage E** — the real grip
importer is `utilization/class_utilization_observable.py` (imports
`grip_store.GripStore`/`get_grip_at`, grip consumed NOT re-fit); the sibling
`reference_utilization_store.py` then *persists* the grip-derived
`g_sigma_onesided` column (it imports no grip module itself).

**Honest measured-NULL (recorded, not a gap):** the grip node was built and
gated, but g4 held-out reconciliation regressed **+155.5% RMS** and g5 synthetic
separability was **31.9% (FAIL)**. The store contract stands and E consumes the
curves, but the grip signal did not clear its own separability bar on this data
— disclosed as-is, per the epic owner's measured-not-hidden rule. Revisiting the
grip fit is future work, not a correction owed by this reconcile.

the per-circuit reference-lap composition and the per-(driver, class) utilization
observables that **stages G/H/PANEL** consume:

- `class_ledger.py` (g1) — `build_weight_matrix` → an `(n, 2+k)` class-weight
  matrix `W` over the **C** segment map (`segment_map.runtime`).
- `reference_lap_product.py` (g2) — `ReferenceLapProduct` / `ConstructorLap` /
  `FieldBasis`; composes the per-constructor and field-reference laps, driving
  `car_prior.build_car_ceiling` → `PhysicsSimulator.simulate_lap`.
- `reference_utilization_store.py` (g2+g3) — `ReferenceUtilizationStore`, its own
  DB `data/reference_utilization.db` with tables `reference_laps` (the
  field-reference **fingerprint**/composition) + `driver_class_observables`
  (persists the grip-derived `g_sigma_onesided` column; imports no grip module).
- `class_utilization_observable.py` (g3) — `build_class_utilization_observables`,
  the per-class deficit observables **G** (`fingerprint.fit`) shrinks; this is the
  real **D**-grip consumer (imports `grip_store.GripStore`/`get_grip_at`, grip
  consumed not re-fit).
- `class_utilization_validation.py` (g4) — the falsifiable validation harness.
- CLI `scripts/build_class_utilization_observables.py` (non-map node).

Consumes **C** `segment_map.runtime` (via g1), `car_prior.build_car_ceiling`,
**D** `grip_store.get_grip_at`, and `layer2.frozen_constants.MAP_STABILITY_DRIFT_M`.
Produces the `reference_laps` composition + `driver_class_observables` that
**G** (`fingerprint.fit`) and **PANEL** (`instrument_panel`) read.

Decision bullets (recorded here, the map's home for per-wave decisions):
- `decision:class-attribution-membership-faithful` — attribution is
  membership-faithful (not distance-weighted). `@grade: settled/measured`.
  This **RETIRES** the #625 `regime_rollup` DISTANCE-share caveat (E's
  field-reference TIME-share composition supersedes it — see the Open Structural
  Questions disposition of `regime_rollup`).
- `decision:field-reference-fingerprint` — the field-reference lap is the
  composition fingerprint. `@grade: guess · settle: g4 validation`.
- `decision:g-one-sided-directed-uncertainty` — the deficit `g` carries a
  one-sided directed uncertainty. `@grade: settled/inherited`.
- Claims `claim:attribution-robust`, `claim:deficits-sum-to-lap`.

### Dependencies (utilization sub-package)

- Reads `struct:physics.layer2` (`estimate_store`/`pool_driver`) read-only via caller-supplied `store_df`.
- Reads `struct:physics.layer2` directly (module-level imports, #628): `pooling.pool_random_effects`
  (`driver_utility.py`'s pooling) and `estimate_store_fields.effective_axis_sigma`/
  `UNRESOLVED_AXIS_SIGMA_FRAC` (`driver_utility.py`'s explicit-unknown widening) — the same
  read-only cross-component edge as above, new evidence, no new edge.
- Reads `struct:physics` simulation/envelope: `capability_envelope.CapabilityEnvelope`,
  `physics_simulator.PhysicsSimulator`, `sim_evaluator.resample_by_progress`, `session_fit.fit_session_full`,
  `session_fit.load_quali_session`, `ribbon.build_session_ribbon`.

# PROBLEM STATEMENT — issue #690

**Reconcile the #664 one-sided grip σ⁺ band scale (whole-lap pace σ) with per-class deficit units.**

Commander run `issue-690`, planning-only engagement (execute and beyond are a separate
engagement). No human reachable: every `user-decision` checkpoint below records the question that
would have been asked, the ruling taken in the human's stead, and the evidence it rests on.

---

## 1. The ask, restated against verified code (not against the issue's framing)

The issue was written at #664 triage time. Since then **#721 landed on `main`**
(`54c7860f`, merging `a5b24249` + `9fae4c9d`) and fixed **two of the three** things the issue text
implies:

| #690's framing | State on `main` today | Residue |
|---|---|---|
| `σ⁺ = hypot(mu, sigma)` folds the ~90 s pace **level** into the band | **FIXED** — `onesided_sigma_from_grip(sigma)` returns `abs(sigma)`; `mu` never enters the scale | none |
| curve evaluated at hardcoded `x=0` | **FIXED** — builder passes `laps=None` → `round(0.5 · cumulative_track_laps_max)` | none |
| whole-lap pace **σ** attached identically to every per-CLASS transit-time deficit | **UNFIXED** | **this issue** |

So #690's real, remaining content is exactly one thing: **the σ⁺ scale is a whole-lap quantity
being written into a per-class row.** Everything else in the issue text is already discharged.

**Confirmed live in real production data** (read-only, archived #670 season run,
`.agent-work/archive/2026-07-27-670-season-run/artifacts/scratch/refutil_season_2023.db`,
2 325 rows):

```
class                  n     avg(g_sigma_onesided)   avg(time_deficit_s)
straight              381   1146998610.5707          1.5332
braking_zone          381   1146998610.5707          0.8848
severity:2023:v1:c0   381   1146998610.5707          3.7457
severity:2023:v1:c1   381   1146998610.5707          0.0036
severity:2023:v1:c2   381   1146998610.5707         -0.0015
severity:2023:v1:c3   381   1146998610.5707          0.1591
```

The σ column is **byte-identical across all six classes** while the deficits it wraps span
0.00–3.75 s. (The 1.1e9 magnitude is the *pre*-#721 store; #721 fixes that magnitude, not this
uniformity. Rebuilding the store does not make the column class-aware.)

And the weights this issue needs **already exist and are already persisted** — `reference_laps`
carries `time_shares_json` per constructor lap and for the field, e.g. Australia-Q:
`straight 0.531 / braking_zone 0.154 / c0 0.162 / c1 0.001 / c2 0.137 / c3 0.015`. The same
quantity is computable in the pure numeric core from `class_ledger.class_time_ledger`
(`time_share_by_class`, structurally summing to 1).

## 2. Success (user-visible outcome) — IQ-001

The `driver_class_observables.g_sigma_onesided` column carries a **per-class** one-sided σ⁺ whose
magnitude is commensurate with that class's own transit-time deficit, such that:

1. the consumer `src/physics/fingerprint/fit.py:_compose_sigma` (which quadrature-adds
   `g_sigma_onesided` per `(driver, class)` cell) stops inflating every cell by the whole-lap
   pace σ;
2. the widths compose back to the lap-level σ under a stated, tested invariant — the direct
   sibling of the map's existing `claim:deficits-sum-to-lap`;
3. the **band-distribution report** W2's acceptance rests on (median / p90 / vacuous count /
   plausible-|D| count) is computed in units that make its numbers comparable at all.

## 3. Protected intent — what must NOT change (IQ-003)

- **The point deficit is untouched.** `speed_deficit_by_class` / `time_deficit_by_class` /
  `lap_time_deficit_s` are byte-identical with and without the G wrap, before and after this
  change. This is the anti-circularity contract (#628) and the module's own binding pre-ruling.
- **μ stays at zero.** Moving the band's centre is #678, explicitly out of scope.
- **G is consumed, never re-fit.** No touch to `grip_baseline.py`, no change to `get_grip_at`'s
  caller-chosen-x contract (its own negative-evidence tests must need zero edits — the same proof
  #721 used).
- **One-sidedness stays.** `decision:g-one-sided-directed-uncertainty` is
  `@grade: settled/inherited` — this issue changes the band's **scale**, not its posture, so no
  decision is being unsettled.
- **No new physical threshold.** A grip-sensitivity model (down-weighting straights because
  rubbering-in doesn't help a power-limited straight) is a modelling claim, not a unit
  reconciliation — recorded as an untaken road, not built.
- **No re-fit, no store schema migration.** Rows are already per `(…, driver, class)`; the column
  already exists. This is a *value* change plus a provenance marker.

## 4. Ambiguities that could make an implementer build the wrong thing (IQ-002) — and the rulings

Each is a decision that would have gone to the human. Ruled here, with the reasoning, per the
engagement's no-human standing instruction.

**D1 — What is the per-class weight?**
*Ruling:* the class's **transit-time share of the lap**, `w_c = t_c / t_lap`, `Σ w_c = 1`
(`class_ledger.class_time_ledger().time_share_by_class`).
*Why:* the issue's own words — "whole-lap pace σ into a per-class **transit-time** band". The σ is
an uncertainty on a lap-**time** level; the deficit it wraps is a class transit **time**; the
unit-coherent bridge between the two is the class's share of lap time. It needs no new physics and
reuses a shipped, invariant-guarded quantity.
`@grade: guess · settle: the band-distribution report's per-class median under time-share vs. the
grip-sensitive variant on the same substrate`

**D2 — Linear share (`w_c·σ`) or quadrature (`√w_c·σ`)?**
*Ruling:* **linear**, `σ⁺_c = w_c · σ_lap`.
*Why:* `get_grip_at` returns **one session-level scalar**. A single common-mode uncertainty
allocated deterministically across the lap contributes `w_c·G` to each class and is *perfectly
correlated* across classes, so the per-class widths **sum** to the lap width. Quadrature encodes an
independence claim (per-class grip errors uncorrelated) that is flatly false for a session-level
grip level, and it would inflate every class (√0.16 = 0.40 ≫ 0.16). Linear is also the only choice
that yields a clean testable invariant. Quadrature recorded as rejected-with-reason.

**D3 — Whose lap supplies the shares: the driver's real lap, the constructor ideal, or the field
reference?**
*Ruling:* the **driver's real lap**, computed in the pure numeric core from `v_real` on the shared
grid.
*Why:* the pure core must stay I/O-free (its stated contract), and the real lap is the one whose
flattery the band is about. The choice is measured **not** load-bearing: the persisted ideal and
field shares differ from each other by <1 % (Australia-Q field `straight` 0.5310 vs Alfa Romeo
0.5319). Document that, don't agonise.

**D4 — Does the store column change meaning, and how does a reader tell?**
*Ruling:* the column keeps its name and gains per-class semantics; `FORMAT_VERSION` bumps
`"1" → "2"` and the column comment states the change.
*Why:* project doctrine is **one canonical path** — a second `g_sigma_onesided_class` column would
create exactly the dual-reader situation `ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md` forbids without a tracked exit.
Nothing reads `format_version` today (verified: written at three sites, gated nowhere), so the
bump is a free, honest provenance marker and not a compatibility fork.

**D5 — Does #690 build the W2 band-distribution report, or inherit it?**
*Ruling:* **build it here, defensively.** #690's routing comment makes the report the stream's
scored artifact "recomputed at each chain step", and says this issue is the unit reconciliation the
report depends on. No such reporter exists anywhere in `src/`, `scripts/` or `tests/` (verified by
search). Every other W2 chain issue (#679, #678, #687, #686, #688) is still OPEN, so nothing will
supply it first. The gate is authored with an explicit precondition: **if a band-distribution
reporter exists at execution time, extend it — do not mint a second one.**

**D6 — Which substrate does the measurement run on?**
*Ruling:* the **archived real #670 season-run stores** (`refutil_season_2023.db` +
`grip_estimates.db` + `segment_maps.db`, 2023-Q, 21 grip sessions / 2 325 class rows), read-only,
copied to scratch. The "W0-stamped substrate" the spec prefers does not exist yet (W0's store
rebuild is unrun). The report **states its substrate and its retained-session fraction** and is
re-runnable against the stamped store the moment it lands. Per T7, the harness **hard-fails** on an
absent store — it must never `pytest.skip` its own evidence away.

**D7 — Does the deficit scale (0.1–0.2 s) gate this issue?**
*Ruling:* **no.** Owner ruling recorded in #724/the spec: the deficit scale is an **aspiration**,
not an acceptance bar; harness *validity* failures are stop-the-line. #690 is accepted on the
scaling being correct, invariant-tested and measured — not on the number it lands at.

## 5. Local evidence that answered instead of asking (IQ-004)

- `main` @ `54c7860f`, `a5b24249` — what #721 actually changed (read as a diff, not assumed).
- `.agent-work/archive/2026-08-01-r3-721-consumer-units/RESULT.md` — the verified consumer topology
  table for `g_sigma_onesided`, and the measured before/after band distribution.
- `.agent-work/archive/2026-08-01-explore-physics-go-forward/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §W2 + the T7/IF15/T19/
  T20/S12/IF6 amendments — the stream's acceptance shape.
- `docs/architecture/packets/physics.md` — stage D→E→G pipeline, `decision:g-one-sided-directed-
  uncertainty`, `claim:deficits-sum-to-lap`.
- The archived season-run DBs — the defect and the weights, both observed directly.

## 6. First independent gate's closing evidence (IQ-005)

`tests/unit/physics/test_class_utilization_observable.py` green **including** the new width-shape
tests, and `tests/unit/physics/test_class_ledger.py` + `tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/test_fit.py`
green unchanged (the consumed-frozen-module guard, `lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests`),
plus a byte-identity assertion that the point deficits did not move.

## 7. Cartographer baseline before planning? (IQ-006)

**No.** `map_orient` RESOLVED against `docs/architecture/index.md` (76 anchors) and the
`struct:physics.utilization` / `struct:physics.layer2` / `struct:physics.fingerprint` packet nodes
are current — #721's own Cartographer pass (`9fae4c9d`) verified this exact area a day ago and
logged a no-op. Reconcile at the end as normal.

## 8. Workflow fit (IQ-007)

Yes for the code gates (small, sharp, independently verifiable, with a real regression surface in a
consumed module). The measurement gate is where the value is: without it this is a plausible-looking
formula change with no evidence behind it.

## 9. Stated non-goals

Re-fitting G (#678/#687); moving μ (#678); the flying-lap gate (#679); condition regressors
(#686/#688); the final consumer contract (#712, owner's decision at W2's close); the
`compose_and_persist_weekend` complexity debt (#722).

---

## Confirmation

**No human reachable.** Sections 2–4 are the confirmation surface; the seven rulings D1–D7 are taken
by the Commander in the human's stead and are re-openable at the plan-approved checkpoint. The
questions as they would have been put to the human are stated verbatim in the D-headings.

independence claim (per-class grip errors uncorrelated) that is flatly false for a session-level
grip level, and it would inflate every class (√0.16 = 0.40 ≫ 0.16). Linear is also the only choice
that yields a clean testable invariant. Quadrature recorded as rejected-with-reason.

**D3 — Whose lap supplies the shares: the driver's real lap, the constructor ideal, or the field
reference?**
*Ruling:* the **driver's real lap**, computed in the pure numeric core from `v_real` on the shared
grid.
*Why:* the pure core must stay I/O-free (its stated contract), and the real lap is the one whose
flattery the band is about. The choice is measured **not** load-bearing: the persisted ideal and
field shares differ from each other by <1 % (Australia-Q field `straight` 0.5310 vs Alfa Romeo
0.5319). Document that, don't agonise.

**D4 — Does the store column change meaning, and how does a reader tell?**
*Ruling:* the column keeps its name and gains per-class semantics; `FORMAT_VERSION` bumps
`"1" → "2"` and the column comment states the change.
*Why:* project doctrine is **one canonical path** — a second `g_sigma_onesided_class` column would
create exactly the dual-reader situation `ORCHESTRATOR_CONTEXT.md` forbids without a tracked exit.
Nothing reads `format_version` today (verified: written at three sites, gated nowhere), so the
bump is a free, honest provenance marker and not a compatibility fork.

**D5 — Does #690 build the W2 band-distribution report, or inherit it?**
*Ruling:* **build it here, defensively.** #690's routing comment makes the report the stream's
scored artifact "recomputed at each chain step", and says this issue is the unit reconciliation the
report depends on. No such reporter exists anywhere in `src/`, `scripts/` or `tests/` (verified by
search). Every other W2 chain issue (#679, #678, #687, #686, #688) is still OPEN, so nothing will
supply it first. The gate is authored with an explicit precondition: **if a band-distribution
reporter exists at execution time, extend it — do not mint a second one.**

**D6 — Which substrate does the measurement run on?**
*Ruling:* the **archived real #670 season-run stores** (`refutil_season_2023.db` +
`grip_estimates.db` + `segment_maps.db`, 2023-Q, 21 grip sessions / 2 325 class rows), read-only,
copied to scratch. The "W0-stamped substrate" the spec prefers does not exist yet (W0's store
rebuild is unrun). The report **states its substrate and its retained-session fraction** and is
re-runnable against the stamped store the moment it lands. Per T7, the harness **hard-fails** on an
absent store — it must never `pytest.skip` its own evidence away.

**D7 — Does the deficit scale (0.1–0.2 s) gate this issue?**
*Ruling:* **no.** Owner ruling recorded in #724/the spec: the deficit scale is an **aspiration**,
not an acceptance bar; harness *validity* failures are stop-the-line. #690 is accepted on the
scaling being correct, invariant-tested and measured — not on the number it lands at.

  uncertainty`, `claim:deficits-sum-to-lap`.

`tests/unit/physics/test_class_utilization_observable.py` green **including** the new width-shape
tests, and `tests/unit/physics/test_class_ledger.py` + `tests/unit/physics/fingerprint/test_fit.py`
green unchanged (the consumed-frozen-module guard, `lesson:consumed-frozen-module-run-guard-tests`),
plus a byte-identity assertion that the point deficits did not move.

**No.** `map_orient` RESOLVED against `docs/architecture/index.md` (76 anchors) and the
`struct:physics.utilization` / `struct:physics.layer2` / `struct:physics.fingerprint` packet nodes
are current — #721's own Cartographer pass (`9fae4c9d`) verified this exact area a day ago and
logged a no-op. Reconcile at the end as normal.

Yes for the code gates (small, sharp, independently verifiable, with a real regression surface in a
consumed module). The measurement gate is where the value is: without it this is a plausible-looking
formula change with no evidence behind it.

Re-fitting G (#678/#687); moving μ (#678); the flying-lap gate (#679); condition regressors
